summary: Guo and Reinecke prove that for a smooth p-adic formal scheme X over O_K (K discretely valued, possibly ramified) the étale realization is an equivalence between analytic prismatic F-crystals and crystalline Z_p-local systems on X_η in Faltings' sense (Theorem A), extending Bhatt–Scholze's theorem for Spf(O_K). Embedding analytic F-crystals into prismatic F-crystals in perfect complexes, they prove étale and crystalline comparisons with coefficients, Poincaré duality for prismatic pushforwards (trace-free and trace-normalized), Frobenius isogeny, a strong étale comparison over 𝔸_inf[1/μ] by an arc-local analysis, and compatibility with filtrations via infinitesimal cohomology over 𝔹⁺_dR, and deduce the relative C_crys conjecture with crystalline coefficients for smooth proper morphisms of formal schemes over ramified bases (Theorem B, Corollary C). The atlas plans the prismatic, A_inf, period-sheaf, crystalline and Bhatt–Scholze inputs; it lacks the higher-dimensional theory (a Part II of PrismaticCohomology), Faltings' crystalline local systems and 𝔹_crys(E) (a Part II of PadicHodgeTheory), convergent isocrystals and Xu/Shiho (source of the rigid-cohomology roadmap), and a few isolated inputs routed to existing proposals. Thirty-six mistakes are recorded (thirty-five by the extraction, one added by the review), including a missing flatness hypothesis in Proposition 3.7, an impossible lift in the proof of Proposition 4.11 for ramified K, an invariant computation in Proposition 2.29 that fails for ramified K, a missing quasi-compactness hypothesis in §2, and gaps in the proofs of Theorems 6.13 and 7.16 and Lemma 9.7; the main theorems survive.

items.name: Fontaine's C_crys conjecture (constant coefficients)
items.statement: For X smooth proper over O_K (K complete discretely valued, perfect residue field k) there is a natural isomorphism H^i(X_{K̄,ét}, Z_p) ⊗_{Z_p} B_crys ≅ H^i_crys(X_s/W(k)) ⊗_{W(k)} B_crys compatible with G_K-actions, Frobenius and (after ⊗ B_dR) filtrations.
items.note: Proved for smooth proper formal O_K-models in CP.2 (BMS1 route); the paper treats it as the constant-coefficient case of Corollary C.

items.name: Theorem A: analytic prismatic F-crystals are crystalline local systems
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K (K complete discretely valued of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field; ramification allowed), with rigid generic fibre X_η. The étale realization T restricts to a natural equivalence T : Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) → Loc^crys_{Z_p}(X_η) between analytic prismatic F-crystals on X and crystalline Z_p-local systems on X_η (in the sense of Faltings, Definition 2.31).
items.locator: Theorem A, p. 3; proved in §§3–4 (Theorem 3.12, Lemma 4.1, Theorems 4.5 and 4.8), pp. 32–47

items.name: Theorem B: relative C_crys conjecture with crystalline coefficients
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of smooth p-adic formal schemes over O_K, let T be a crystalline sheaf of Ẑ_p-modules on X_η (Definition 2.31), and let (E_s, φ_{E_s}, Fil^•(E)) be the associated filtered F-isocrystal on (X_s/W(k))_crys. Then for every i the higher direct image R^i f_{η,*}T is a crystalline sheaf of Ẑ_p-modules on Y_η, associated (in the sense of Faltings, Definition 2.31) with the filtered F-isocrystal R^i f_{s,crys,*} E_s.
items.locator: Theorem B, p. 3; proved pp. 92–93 from Theorems 9.15 and 10.13

items.name: Corollary C: absolute C_crys conjecture with crystalline coefficients
items.statement: Let X be a smooth proper p-adic formal scheme over O_K and T a crystalline sheaf of Ẑ_p-modules on X_η with associated filtered F-isocrystal E_s. Then for every i there is a natural isomorphism of B_crys-modules H^i(X_C, T) ⊗_{Z_p} B_crys ≅ H^i_crys(X_s/W(k), E_s) ⊗_{W(k)} B_crys, where X_C = X_η ×_K C is the geometric generic fibre, compatible with the G_K-actions, Frobenius and filtrations.
items.note: Printed with H^i(X_η, T) on the left (sourceIssues E1).

items.name: Corollary 1.17: p-adic Poincaré duality for crystalline local systems
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of smooth formal O_K-schemes of relative equidimension n and T a crystalline Z_p-local system on X_η. There is a natural perfect pairing of Z_p-lisse complexes Rf_{η,*}T ⊗^L_{Ẑ_{p,Y_η}} Rf_{η,*}T^∨ → Ẑ_{p,Y_η}(−n)[−2n].
items.locator: Corollary 1.17, p. 8 (from Theorem 7.16 by étale realization)

items.name: Du–Liu–Moon–Shimizu: completed prismatic F-crystals and crystalline local systems
items.statement: For X smooth over O_K, effective (completed) prismatic F-crystals on X correspond to crystalline Z_p-local systems on X_η with non-negative Hodge–Tate weights; Breuil–Kisin and Tate twists extend this to all analytic prismatic F-crystals; analytic prismatic F-crystals need not extend to prismatic F-crystals in vector bundles ([DLMS22, Ex. 3.35]); the higher-dimensional Breuil–Kisin prisms (R̃⟦u⟧, (E(u))) of a framed smooth affine are weakly final in X_Δ.
items.locator: Remarks 1.4, 1.9, p. 4–5; proof of Theorem 5.10, p. 51; proof of Proposition 9.9, p. 86, citing [DLMS22, Thm 1.3, Ex. 3.35, Rem. 1.5, Def. 4.?]
items.note: Independent parallel proof of Theorem A; its Breuil–Kisin prisms are used in §5 and its projectivity of φ-modules of finite E-height in §9.

items.name: A_inf(O_C), q, μ, ξ̃ and the Hodge–Tate specialization θ̃
items.statement: Fix compatible p^n-th roots of unity ζ_{p^n} ∈ O_C and ε = (1, ζ_p, ζ_{p^2}, …) ∈ O_C^♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} O_C/p. A_inf = A_inf(O_C) := W(O_C^♭), q := [ε], μ := q − 1, ξ̃ := [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1); then φ(μ) = μ·ξ̃. (A_inf, (ξ̃)) is a prism; the quotient map A_inf → A_inf/ξ̃ = O_C is the Hodge–Tate specialization θ̃. The de Rham specialization is θ := θ̃∘φ, with prism (A_inf, ker θ) as in [BS22, Thm. 3.10]. The morphism from the initial prism (Δ_{O_C}, I) → (A_inf, ξ̃) (given by φ) is an isomorphism and the two are identified. B^+_dR := B^+_dR(O_C) := (A_inf[1/p])^∧_{ξ̃} (completion at ker θ̃, not at ker θ as in [Fon82]).
items.note: Mathlib has A_inf = 𝕎(O_C^♭) with Fontaine's θ (mathlib:WittVector.fontaineTheta); the q-notation and θ̃ = θ∘φ⁻¹ are AI.0's normalization interface.

items.name: Period rings of a quasiregular semiperfectoid O_C-algebra
items.statement: For S quasiregular semiperfectoid over O_C with initial prism (Δ_S, I): A_inf(S) = Δ_S, A_crys(S) = Δ_S{I/p} (the p-completed PD envelope of ker θ), φ*A_crys(S) = Δ_S{φ(I)/p}, Δ_S⟨I/p⟩ = (Δ_S[I/p])^∧_p, and B⁺_dR(S) = Δ_S[1/p]^∧_I ≅ (Δ_S⟨I/p⟩[1/p])^∧_I, with the Frobenius-equivariant maps of the diagram on p. 11.
items.note: Printed with Δ_S⟨I/p⟩ := Δ_S[1/p]^∧_p (sourceIssues E5). A_crys(S) = Δ_S{I/p} is BS22 Cor. 2.39/Prop. 7.10 (PR.2); the diagram follows BS23 Constr. 6.2 (PR.7).

items.name: Prisms and their variants
items.statement: Prisms (A, I) (A a δ-ring, I a Cartier divisor, A derived (p,I)-complete, p ∈ I + φ(I)A), bounded, perfect, crystalline ((A,(p))), and Breuil–Kisin prisms (W(k)⟦u⟧, (E(u))), with maps of prisms; the notation A{f_i} for δ-envelopes and A⟨I/p⟩ for the p-completion of A[I/p].

items.name: Bhatt–Scholze comparison theorems for prismatic cohomology
items.statement: For a bounded prism (A,I) and X smooth p-adic formal over Ā: the Hodge–Tate comparison (H^i of the reduction mod I is Ω^i{−i}, with the map of topoi ν : Shv(X_Δ) → Shv(X_ét)), the crystalline comparison for I = (p), the de Rham comparison after φ_A-twisted reduction, the étale comparison RΓ_ét(X_{A[1/I]}, Z/p^n) ≅ (RΓ_Δ(X/A)/p^n[1/I])^{φ=1} for perfect (A,I), completed base change, and perfectness for proper X.
items.locator: §1, p. 2 and passim, citing [BS22, Thm 1.8, Thm 4.11, Thm 5.2, Constr. 4.4]

items.name: Frobenius isogeny and Nygaard factorization for prismatic cohomology of O
items.statement: For X smooth proper over Ā the linearized Frobenius φ_A^*RΓ_Δ(X/A)[1/I] → RΓ_Δ(X/A)[1/I] is an isomorphism (Lη_I-factorization), and for quasiregular semiperfect R the Frobenius on Δ_R factors through the Nygaard filtration.
items.locator: §1, p. 7; proof of Proposition 6.? (qrsp factorization), p. 58; Remark 8.10, citing [BS22, Thm 1.16, Thm 15.3]

items.name: Perfect prisms and perfectoid rings; perfections of prisms
items.statement: (A,I) ↦ A/I is an equivalence between perfect prisms and perfectoid rings; every prism has a (completed) perfection, universal among maps to perfect prisms; a perfect prism is initial among prisms over its perfectoid quotient.

items.name: Initial prisms of quasiregular semiperfectoid rings and quasi-syntomic descent
items.statement: For S quasiregular semiperfectoid, Spf(S)_Δ has an initial prism (Δ_S, I); for S over a perfectoid R, Δ_R → Δ_S is (p,I)-completely faithfully flat; quasi-syntomic covers lift to prismatic covers; crystals on X_Δ are equivalent to modules over Δ_• on X_qrsp; large quasi-syntomic algebras; completed base change commutes with totalizations.

items.name: arc-descent for the prismatic structure sheaf on perfectoid rings
items.statement: O : S ↦ A_inf(S) (and W_r) satisfies arc-descent on p-complete perfectoid rings, and every perfectoid ring admits a p-complete arc-cover by a product of perfectoid valuation rings of rank ≤ 1 with algebraically closed fraction fields.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 3.13, Theorem 9.1, Proposition 7.1, pp. 33, 63, 81, citing [BS22, Prop. 8.10, Rmk 8.8], [ČS23, Lem. 2.2.3]

items.name: δ-structures along étale maps, prismatic and PD envelopes
items.statement: δ-structures extend uniquely along (p,I)-completely étale maps; prismatic envelopes of regular ideals are flat; the PD envelope of (p, d) is the δ-envelope A{φ(d)/p} ([BS22, Cor. 2.39]); flat descent for O on X_Δ.

items.name: Absolute prismatic site, Breuil–Kisin twists and Hodge–Tate crystals (Bhatt–Lurie)
items.statement: The absolute prismatic site X_Δ with its structure sheaves, Breuil–Kisin twists O_Δ{n}, the Hodge–Tate gerbe and the description of Hodge–Tate crystals as modules with a Sen operator, the big crystalline site with the p-completely flat topology in which A_crys(R) is initial for R quasiregular semiperfect, and quasi-syntomic descent for crystalline cohomology.

items.name: Prismatic F-crystals in vector bundles and perfect complexes
items.statement: A prismatic F-crystal on X is a crystal E of vector bundles (resp. perfect complexes) on (X_Δ, O_Δ) with an isomorphism φ_E : (φ*E)[1/I_Δ] ≅ E[1/I_Δ]; Laurent F-crystals are the analogous objects over O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p.

items.name: Bhatt–Scholze: prismatic F-crystals over O_K and crystalline representations
items.statement: For X = Spf(O_K) the étale realization Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Rep^crys_{Z_p}(G_K) is an equivalence onto Z_p-lattices in crystalline representations.
items.locator: Theorem 1.2, p. 2; used in Proposition 3.8 and Theorem 4.5, citing [BS23, Thm 1.2]

items.name: Laurent F-crystals are étale Z_p-local systems (derived form)
items.statement: For a bounded p-adic formal scheme X, Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p) ≅ Loc_{Z_p}(X_η), and derived D^φ_perf(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p) ≅ D^b_lisse(X_η, Z_p) (the derived étale realization T), compatibly with perfections, with invariance of unit F-crystals under completed perfection and with the F_p-Riemann–Hilbert correspondence in characteristic p.
items.locator: §1, p. 4; Constructions 3.9, Remarks 3.10–3.11, pp. 31–32; §5–6, pp. 55–56, citing [BS23, Cor. 3.8, Prop. 3.?, Notation]

items.name: Bhatt–Scholze étale realization and its properties
items.statement: The étale realization Vect^φ(X_Δ) → Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) of [BS23, Constr. 4.8], injectivity of A → A[1/I]^∧_p for p-torsionfree qrsp S ([BS23, Lem. 4.11]), compatibility with Breuil–Kisin/Tate twists ([BS23, Ex. 4.6, 4.9]).

items.name: Bhatt–Scholze: from filtered φ-modules to F-crystals and the boundary analysis
items.statement: Over O_K: the F-crystal over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p] attached to a filtered φ-module, its analytic continuation to Δ_•⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/p], the identification of B⁺_dR(S) via rational localizations, the structure of the prism of O_C ⊗̂_{O_K} O_C and boundedness of descent data at the boundary.
items.locator: §4, pp. 40–46, citing [BS23, Constr. 6.?, Rem. 6.?, Lem. 6.7, Prop. 6.?]

items.name: Beilinson fibre square
items.statement: For qrsp S over O_C the Beilinson fibre square relating Δ_S, its Nygaard completion, A_crys and B_dR^+ (rationally), used to analyse the prism of S ⊗̂_R S.

items.name: Beauville–Laszlo gluing
items.statement: For a ring A, f ∈ A a nonzerodivisor, modules over A[1/f] and over the f-adic completion with an isomorphism over Â[1/f] glue to an A-module; vector bundles glue likewise.

items.name: Breuil–Kisin–Fargues modules and Fargues' theorem
items.statement: BKF modules over A_inf (finitely presented, finite free after p-inversion, with φ-isomorphism after inverting ξ̃), their étale lattice T (BMS18 Lem. 4.26), vector bundles on the punctured spectrum of A_inf (Lem. 4.6), the intersection formula ⋂_r (μ/φ^{-r}(μ))A_inf = μA_inf (Lem. 3.23), coherence of W_r(O) and perfectness of finitely presented A_inf-modules finite free after inverting p, and full faithfulness of Fargues' functor to pairs (T, Ξ) (BMS18 Thm 4.28).

items.name: A_inf-cohomology of smooth proper formal schemes
items.statement: For X smooth proper over O_C, RΓ_{A_inf}(X) is perfect and its top-degree cohomology is free of rank one when X is geometrically connected.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 7.1, p. 63, citing [BMS18, Thm 14.5]

items.name: The pro-étale site of a rigid space and affinoid perfectoids
items.statement: For an adic space X_η over Spa(K,O_K), the pro-étale site X_{η,proét} (Scholze), in which affinoid perfectoid objects form a basis.

items.name: Lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves and étale Z_p-local systems on rigid spaces
items.statement: Ẑ_p = lim Z/p^n on X_{η,proét}; a lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf is locally Ẑ_p ⊗ M for M finitely generated over Z_p; Z_p-local systems are the torsion-free ones; D^b_lisse(X_η, Z_p).

items.name: Perfectoid algebras and affinoid perfectoid spaces
items.statement: Perfectoid Tate algebras and affinoid perfectoid spaces over C, their tilts.

items.name: Infinitesimal and de Rham period sheaves in the Hodge–Tate normalization
items.statement: On X_{η,proét}: 𝔸_inf = W(R^{+,♭}), 𝔹_inf, O𝔹_inf; 𝔹⁺_dR, 𝔹_dR, O𝔹⁺_dR, O𝔹_dR completed along ker θ̃ (θ̃ = θ∘φ⁻¹) rather than ker θ, with the t-adic filtrations and the 𝔹⁺_dR-linear connection on O𝔹_dR satisfying Griffiths transversality; local structure of O𝔹⁺_dR as a power series ring over 𝔹⁺_dR.
items.locator: Definitions 2.2–2.3 and Warning 2.4, pp. 12–13, citing [Sch13, Def. 6.1, 6.8, Cor. 6.13, Prop. 6.10]
items.note: The scalar extension defining O𝔹⁺_dR needs the φ-twisted W(k)-structure on 𝔸_inf (sourceIssues E6).

items.name: Crystalline period sheaves
items.statement: 𝔸_crys, 𝔹⁺_crys, 𝔹_crys on X_{η,proét} (Tan–Tong), with Frobenius and filtration.

items.name: Relative fundamental exact sequence for crystalline period sheaves
items.statement: 0 → Q̂_p → 𝔹_crys^{φ=1} → 𝔹_dR/𝔹⁺_dR → 0 on X_{η,proét} (Brinon's relative version).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.22(ii), p. 17, citing [Bri08, Prop. 6.2.?]

items.name: Scholze's relative de Rham comparison and finiteness
items.statement: For f : X → Y proper smooth of rigid spaces and L a de Rham (lisse) Ẑ_p-sheaf: R^i f_*L is lisse, ν_*(E ⊗ O𝔹_dR) recovers E, and R^i f_*L ⊗ O𝔹_dR ≅ R^i f_{dR,*}(E,∇) ⊗ O𝔹_dR compatibly with filtrations and connections.

items.name: Tate's theorem and Fontaine's period rings
items.statement: H^0(G_K, C(r)) = K for r = 0 and 0 otherwise; Fontaine's A_inf, A_crys, B_crys, B_dR, crystalline representations and D_crys.

items.name: Weakly admissible filtered φ-modules are admissible
items.statement: Colmez–Fontaine/Kedlaya: weakly admissible filtered φ-modules over K arise from crystalline representations (slope filtration).

items.name: Crystalline site, crystals and crystalline cohomology
items.statement: Berthelot's (big) crystalline site (X/(A,J,γ))_crys, crystals, and crystalline cohomology H^i(X/W(k)_crys); relative crystalline pushforwards Rf_{crys,*}.

items.name: crystal in coherent sheaves on the crystalline site
items.statement: Let X_s be a k-scheme, V_0 = W(k) with its standard pd-structure, (X_s/V_0)_crys the big crystalline site. A crystal (in coherent sheaves) on X_s is a sheaf E of O_{X_s/V_0}-modules such that (i) for every pd-thickening (U,T,γ), E|_T is a coherent O_T-module, and (ii) for every morphism α : (U,T,γ) → (U',T',γ'), the map α^*(E|_{T'}) → E|_T is an O_T-linear isomorphism.

items.name: isocrystal
items.statement: The category Isoc(X_s/V_0) of isocrystals has as objects the crystals on X_s and morphisms Hom_{Isoc}(E,E') := Hom_{O_{X_s/V_0}}(E,E') ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p.

items.name: Frobenius endomorphism of the crystalline site
items.statement: The absolute Frobenius of X_s and the Witt vector Frobenius of V_0 induce a continuous and cocontinuous morphism of sites F : (X_s/V_0)_crys → (X_s/V_0)_crys (and of topoi), also denoted F.

items.name: F-isocrystal and its tensor structure
items.statement: An F-isocrystal on X_s is a pair (E, φ) with E an isocrystal and φ : F^*E → E an isomorphism; morphisms are morphisms of isocrystals α with α∘φ = φ'∘F^*α. The category Isoc^φ(X_s/V_0) is symmetric closed monoidal: (E,φ) ⊗ (E',φ') = (E⊗E', φ⊗φ'), and the internal hom 𝓗om(E,E') has F-structure F^*𝓗om(E,E') ≃ 𝓗om(F^*E, F^*E') → 𝓗om(E,E'), g ↦ φ_{E'}∘g∘φ_E^{-1}.

items.name: Crystals as modules with topologically quasi-nilpotent connection
items.statement: Let X̃ = Spf R be affine smooth over V_0 and E a crystal on X̃_s. Then E(X̃) := lim_r E(X̃_s, X̃ ⊗_{V_0} V_0/p^r, γ) (γ the canonical pd-structure on pR/p^rR) is a finitely presented R-module with a canonical connection, and this gives an equivalence between crystals on X̃_s and finitely presented R-modules M with a flat, topologically quasi-nilpotent connection ∇ : M → M ⊗_R Ω^1_R. Topological quasi-nilpotence: for a local framing with basis dx_i of Ω^1_R and ∇ = Σ θ_i ⊗ dx_i, for each i and m ∈ M one has θ_i^n(m) ∈ pM for n ≫ 0.

items.name: Frobenius lifts on smooth affine formal V_0-schemes
items.statement: If X̃ = Spf R is a smooth affine p-adic formal scheme over V_0 with special fibre X̃_s = X̃ ⊗ k, the absolute Frobenius of X̃_s lifts (non-uniquely) to an endomorphism of X̃, since the obstruction group Ext^1(LF^*L_{X̃_s/k}, O_{X̃_s}) ≃ Ext^1(F^*Ω^1_{X̃_s/k}, O_{X̃_s}) vanishes (X̃_s smooth affine).

items.name: Framings of smooth formal schemes
items.statement: Let X be a smooth affine formal scheme over Spf O_K. A framing of X is an étale morphism X → Spf O_K⟨x_1^{±1}, …, x_d^{±1}⟩ over Spf O_K for some d ≥ 0.

items.name: Lemma 2.10: local framings exist
items.statement: A smooth formal scheme X → Spf O_K has a basis of affine open formal subschemes that admit a framing.

items.name: Topological invariance of the étale site
items.statement: For a nilpotent (or henselian) thickening, étale (finite étale) algebras correspond; used for unramified models and finite étale lifts along (A, I).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 2.9, p. 14; §7, p. 70, citing [SP22, Tag 039R]

items.name: Berthelot: Poincaré duality for crystalline cohomology
items.statement: Poincaré duality for crystalline cohomology (of crystals on smooth proper schemes in characteristic p).

items.name: Berthelot–Ogus: Frobenius isogeny on crystalline cohomology
items.statement: For the structure sheaf O_crys (smooth proper X over a perfect field) Frobenius acts on crystalline cohomology as an isogeny (via gauges).

items.name: Ogus's convergent site and convergent isocrystals
items.statement: Ogus's convergent site (X/V_0)_conv (enlargements) and its crystals, identified with Berthelot's convergent isocrystals.

items.name: isocrystals give vector bundles with p-adically convergent connection
items.statement: If E is an isocrystal on X̃_s, Construction 2.11 gives a finite projective R[1/p]-module, i.e. an O_{X̃_η}-vector bundle E on X̃_η = X̃ ×_{Spf V_0} Spa(K_0,V_0) with flat connection ∇ : E → E ⊗ Ω^1_{X̃_η/K_0}; it carries a complete norm ‖·‖ unique up to equivalence. With a framing, topological quasi-nilpotence gives lim_{|α|→∞} ‖θ^α(e)‖ = 0 for e ∈ Γ(X̃_η, E), and since |p^n/n!| is bounded (ramification index of V_0 is 1 ≤ p−1), lim_{|α|→∞} ‖θ^α(e)/α!‖·|p|^{|α|} = 0.

items.name: convergent connection
items.statement: Let X̃ = Spf R be affine smooth over V_0 and E a coherent module (a finitely presented R[1/p]-module with complete norm ‖·‖). A flat connection ∇ : E → E ⊗ Ω^1_{X̃_η/K_0} is convergent if for all e ∈ Γ(X̃_η, E) and all 0 ≤ η < 1, lim_{|α|→∞} ‖θ^α(e)/α!‖·η^{|α|} = 0 in local coordinates (∇ = Σ θ_i ⊗ dx_i, multi-index notation). This is independent of coordinates (Remark 2.13, via [Ber96, Def. 2.2.5]).

items.name: Berthelot: F-isocrystals = vector bundles with convergent connection and Frobenius
items.statement: Let X̃ = Spf R be an affine smooth p-adic formal scheme over V_0, X̃_s = X̃ ⊗ k, X̃_η = X̃ ×_{Spf V_0} Spa(K_0,V_0), and fix a lift F of absolute Frobenius to X̃. The functor (E, φ) ↦ the vector bundle with connection on X̃_η given by E(X̃)[1/p] = (lim_r E(X̃_s, X̃ ⊗ V_0/p^r, γ))[1/p] is an equivalence between Isoc^φ(X̃_s/V_0) and the category of O_{X̃_η}-vector bundles E with flat convergent connection ∇ and an isomorphism φ : F^*E → E compatible with the connections.

items.name: F-isocrystals are convergent; invariance under X_s ⊂ X_{p=0}
items.statement: Ogus's convergent site (X̃/V_0)_conv: its crystals are Berthelot's convergent isocrystals. Any F-isocrystal on X̃_s extends (by Dwork's Frobenius trick) to a convergent isocrystal on (X̃_{p=0}/V_0)_conv. Consequently, for X smooth over O_K, the inclusions (X_s/V_0)_crys ⊂ (X_{p=0}/V_0)_crys ⊂ (X_{p=0}/V_0)_conv induce equivalences Isoc^φ((X_s/V_0)_crys) ≃ Isoc^φ((X_{p=0}/V_0)_crys) ≃ Isoc^φ((X_{p=0}/V_0)_conv), with inverses given by restriction; the same holds for F-isocrystals in perfect complexes.

items.name: underlying vector bundle of a convergent isocrystal
items.statement: Let X be a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_K with rigid generic fibre X_η and E a convergent isocrystal on (X_{p=0}/V_0)_conv. There is a vector bundle with flat connection (E = E(X, X_{p=0}), ∇) on X_η.

items.name: local description of the underlying vector bundle
items.statement: In the situation of (i), assume E underlies an F-isocrystal on (X_s/V_0)_crys (Remark 2.15). For every V_0-model Ũ of an affine open U ⊂ X, (E,∇)|_{U_η} ≅ (E(Ũ), ∇_Ũ) ⊗_{V_0} K, where (E(Ũ), ∇_Ũ) is the bundle with connection of Theorem 2.14.

items.name: underlying vector bundle (with connection) of a convergent isocrystal
items.statement: (E, ∇) from Proposition 2.17 is called the underlying vector bundle of E; by Remark 2.15 this applies to F-isocrystals (E, φ) on X_s.

items.name: Ogus: convergent isocrystals on a smooth V_0-model
items.statement: For X̃ = Spf R^+ smooth over V_0, a convergent isocrystal E corresponds to a vector bundle Ẽ = E(X̃)[1/p] on X̃_η with (convergent) connection ∇̃, and Γ(((R^+ ⊗ k)/V_0)_conv, E)[1/p] ≃ Ẽ(X̃_η)^{∇=0}.

items.name: unramified model of a framed formal scheme
items.statement: Let X be a smooth affine formal scheme over O_K with a framing □ : X → Spf O_K⟨x_1^{±1},…,x_d^{±1}⟩. Then there is a unique (up to unique isomorphism) smooth affine formal scheme X̃ over V_0 with a framing □̃ : X̃ → Spf V_0⟨x_1^{±1},…,x_d^{±1}⟩ whose base change to Spf O_K is □.

items.name: Tan–Tong description of F-isocrystals
items.statement: Locally for framed X̃ with Frobenius lift, F-isocrystals are equivalently vector bundles E on X̃_η with flat convergent connection ∇ and a Frobenius morphism F^*E → E.

items.name: filtered F-isocrystal
items.statement: Let X be a smooth formal scheme over Spf O_K, X_s := X_red, X_η := X ×_{Spf O_K} Spa(K,O_K). A filtered F-isocrystal on X is a triple (E, φ, Fil^•(E)) with (E, φ) an F-isocrystal on X_s and Fil^•(E) a separated, exhaustive, locally split, decreasing filtration of the underlying vector bundle (E, ∇) satisfying Griffiths transversality ∇(Fil^r E) ⊂ Fil^{r−1}E ⊗ Ω^1_{X_η}. They form a symmetric closed monoidal category fIsoc^φ(X_s/V_0), with Fil^r(E ⊗ E') = Σ_i Fil^{−i}E ⊗ Fil^{i+r}E' and Fil^r 𝓗om(E,E')(U_η) = {s : s(Fil^iE(U_η)) ⊂ Fil^{i+r}E'(U_η) ∀ i}.

items.name: filtered map φ^*𝔹_crys → 𝔹_dR
items.statement: With the paper's (ker θ̃-completed) de Rham sheaves there is a natural filtered map φ^*_{𝔸_inf}𝔹_crys → 𝔹_dR.

items.name: K-linear crystalline period sheaves
items.statement: 𝔸_{inf,K} := 𝔸_inf ⊗_W O_K with surjection θ_K : 𝔸_{inf,K}(R,R^+) → R^+; 𝔸_{crys,K} := 𝔸_crys ⊗_W O_K; 𝔹^+_{crys,K} := 𝔸_{crys,K}[1/p] = 𝔹^+_crys ⊗_{K_0} K; 𝔹_{crys,K} := 𝔹^+_{crys,K}[1/t] = 𝔹_crys ⊗_{K_0} K.

items.name: injectivity of 𝔹_{crys,K} → 𝔹_dR
items.statement: There are natural maps of sheaves of rings on X_{η,proét}: 𝔹_{crys,K} → φ^*_{𝔸_inf}𝔹_{crys,K} → 𝔹_dR, which are injective and compatible with the maps from 𝔹_crys.

items.name: fundamental exact sequence (sheaf version)
items.statement: The sequence 0 → Q̂_p → (𝔹_crys)^{φ=1} → 𝔹_dR/𝔹^+_dR → 0 of sheaves on X_{η,proét} is exact.

items.name: Shimizu: B^+_dR is insensitive to K-linearization
items.statement: The natural map 𝔹^+_dR → 𝔹^+_{dR,K} (formal completion of 𝔸_{inf,K}[1/p] along the K-linearized specialization) is a filtered isomorphism (completeness plus isomorphism on graded pieces).

items.name: Shimizu/Brinon: injectivity of B^+_crys ⊗ K into B^+_dR
items.statement: 𝔹^+_crys ⊗_{K_0} K → 𝔹^+_max ⊗_{K_0} K is injective, and 𝔹^+_max ⊗_{K_0} K → (𝔸_{inf,K}[1/p])^∧_{ker θ} is injective.

items.name: intersection formula for Fil 𝔹_crys
items.statement: The injections 𝔹_crys → 𝔹_{crys,K} → 𝔹_dR ≃ 𝔹_{dR,K} are filtered, and Fil^r 𝔹_crys = Fil^r 𝔹_dR ∩ 𝔹_crys. Consequently, for affinoid perfectoid (R,R^+) over X_η, Fil^r 𝔹_{crys,K}(R,R^+) contains every Σ_{i≥r} a_i ξ^{[i]} with (a_i) ⊂ 𝔸_inf(R,R^+)[1/p] p-adically convergent (ξ a generator of ker θ).

items.name: filtration on 𝔹_{crys,K}
items.statement: Fil^r 𝔹_{crys,K} := Fil^r 𝔹_dR ∩ 𝔹_{crys,K} for r ∈ Z (via the injection of Lemma 2.22(i)).

items.name: 𝔹_crys(E) for an F-isocrystal E
items.statement: Assume X_η is the rigid generic fibre of a smooth formal O_K-scheme X, X_s = X_red. For E ∈ Isoc^φ(X_s/V_0) (extended to (X_{p=0}/V_0)_crys by Remark 2.15) and U ∈ Perfd/X_{η,proét} with Û = Spa(S,S^+), S a perfectoid C-algebra, using the pro-pd-thickening 𝔸_crys(S,S^+) → S^+/p in (X_{p=0}/V_0)_crys: 𝔹^+_crys(E)(U) := E(𝔸_crys(S,S^+))[1/p] = (lim_r E(S^+/p, 𝔸_crys(S,S^+)/p^r, γ))[1/p], γ the canonical pd-structure; 𝔹_crys(E)(U) := 𝔹^+_crys(E)(U)[1/μ]. 𝔹^+_{crys,K}(E), 𝔹_{crys,K}(E) are the K-linear base extensions and 𝔹_dR(E) := 𝔹_crys(E) ⊗_{𝔹_crys} 𝔹_dR.
items.note: Printed text differs: (printed with 𝔸_crys(S,S^+)/p in place of S^+/p (sourceIssues E7))

items.name: 𝔹_crys(E) is a sheaf
items.statement: The functors 𝔹^+_crys(E) and 𝔹_crys(E) of Definition 2.25 are sheaves on Perfd/X_{η,proét}.

items.name: Frobenius on 𝔹_crys(E)
items.statement: 𝔹_crys(E) is a 𝔹_crys-module, and for the Frobenius F of 𝔹_crys there is a canonical isomorphism F^*𝔹_crys(E) ≃ 𝔹_crys(F^*E); hence for (E,φ) ∈ Isoc^φ(X_s/V_0) one gets a Frobenius isomorphism φ : F^*𝔹_crys(E) ≃ 𝔹_crys(F^*E) → 𝔹_crys(E).

items.name: filtration on 𝔹_{crys,K}(E)
items.statement: Let (E, φ, Fil^•E) be a filtered F-isocrystal. Assume X affine with V_0-model X̃ = Spf R^+ and framing V_0⟨x_i^{±1}⟩ → R^+, and that S^+ contains compatible p-power roots x_i^♭ of the x_i. By formal étaleness (ker(𝔸_crys(S,S^+)/p^n → S^+/p^n) is nil), x_i ↦ [x_i^♭] extends to s : R^+ → 𝔸_crys(S,S^+); the crystal property gives E(𝔸_crys(S,S^+))[1/μ] ⊗_{K_0} K ≃ E(R^+) ⊗_{R^+,s} 𝔹_{crys,K}(S,S^+) ≃ E(R_K) ⊗_{O(X_η),s} 𝔹_{crys,K}(S,S^+), and Fil^• on 𝔹_{crys,K}(E)(S,S^+) is the tensor product of Fil^•E and Fil^•𝔹_{crys,K} (Definition 2.23). It is independent of s: for another s' the transition isomorphism is c(e ⊗ 1) = Σ_α θ^α(e) ⊗ (s(x) − s'(x))^{[α]}, filtered by Griffiths transversality provided s(x_i) − s'(x_i) ∈ Fil^1𝔸_crys. Since x_i^♭ exist pro-étale locally, the filtrations glue to a filtration on 𝔹_{crys,K}(E).
items.note: The printed independence argument allows lifts s′ that agree with s only modulo p (sourceIssues E8); the construction's own lifts satisfy θ∘s′ = structure map, and the statement above is written with that hypothesis.

items.name: filtration on 𝔹_dR(E) and filtered base change
items.statement: Locally choosing a map O(X) → 𝔹^+_dR(S,S^+) lifting the structure map O(X) → S, 𝔹_dR(E)(S,S^+) gets the tensor product filtration of Fil^•E and Fil^•𝔹_dR(S,S^+); by Griffiths transversality this is independent of the choice. The map 𝔹_{crys,K}(E) → 𝔹_dR(E) is filtered and Fil^•𝔹_dR(E) ≃ Fil^•𝔹_{crys,K}(E) ⊗_{Fil^•𝔹_{crys,K}} Fil^•𝔹_dR.

items.name: filtered φ-vector bundles over 𝔹_crys
items.statement: fVect^φ(X_η, 𝔹_crys) denotes the category of 𝔹_crys-vector bundles on X_{η,proét} with Frobenius structure and with a filtration (after ⊗_{K_0}K) compatible with that of 𝔹_{crys,K}.

items.name: global sections of an isocrystal via 𝔹_crys
items.statement: Let X be a quasi-compact smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K, E a convergent isocrystal on (X_{p=0}/V_0)_conv and 𝔹_crys(E) as in Definition 2.25. There is an isomorphism Γ((X_{p=0}/V_0)_conv, E)[1/p] ≅ Γ(X_{η,proét}, 𝔹_crys(E)), natural in X and E; it is Frobenius-equivariant (resp. filtered after ⊗_{K_0}K) when E has a Frobenius structure (resp. a filtration).
items.note: Quasi-compactness is needed for the reduction to affines (sourceIssues E10); the proof's invariant computation must be corrected when K ≠ K_0 (sourceIssues E9).

items.name: Hom of filtered F-isocrystals via 𝔹_crys
items.statement: Let X be a quasi-compact smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K and E_i = (E_i, φ_i, Fil^•(E_i)), i = 1,2, filtered F-isocrystals on X_s. There is a natural isomorphism of Q_p-vector spaces Hom_{fIsoc^φ(X_{p=0}/V_0)}(E_1,E_2) ≅ Hom_{fVect^φ(X_η, 𝔹_crys)}(𝔹_crys(E_1), 𝔹_crys(E_2)).
items.note: Quasi-compactness added (sourceIssues E10).

items.name: weakly crystalline sheaf (Faltings)
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K, X_s its reduced special fibre, X_η its generic fibre (adic space over Spa(K,O_K)). A sheaf of Ẑ_p-modules L on X_{η,proét} is weakly crystalline if (i) L is lisse (pro-étale locally Ẑ_p ⊗_{Z_p} M, M finitely generated) and (ii) there are an F-isocrystal (E, φ) on X_s (Definition 2.7) and an isomorphism ϑ : 𝔹_crys(E) ≅ 𝔹_crys ⊗_{Ẑ_p} L such that (a) ϑ commutes with the Frobenius isomorphisms (Remark 2.27). If L is torsionfree it is a weakly crystalline local system.

items.name: crystalline sheaf / crystalline local system (Faltings)
items.statement: L as above is crystalline if moreover (E, φ) underlies a filtered F-isocrystal (E, φ, Fil^•(E)) (Definition 2.18) and (b) ϑ_K := ϑ ⊗_{K_0} K : 𝔹_crys(E) ⊗_{K_0} K ≅ (𝔹_crys ⊗_{K_0} K) ⊗_{Ẑ_p} L carries the filtration of Construction 2.28 onto the filtration coming from the first factor. (E, φ, Fil^•E) is then said to be associated with L. If L is torsionfree, it is a crystalline local system; Loc^crys_{Z_p}(X_η) denotes their category.

items.name: de Rham sheaf / de Rham local system
items.statement: Assume X_η smooth over Spa(K,O_K). A sheaf of Ẑ_p-modules L on X_{η,proét} is de Rham if (i) L is lisse and (ii) there exist a locally free O_{X_η}-module E with a separated, exhaustive, locally split, decreasing filtration Fil^•E and a flat connection ∇ : E → E ⊗ Ω^1_{X_η} with ∇(Fil^iE) ⊂ Fil^{i−1}E ⊗ Ω^1_{X_η} for all i ∈ Z, such that L ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹^+_dR ≃ (Fil^0(E ⊗_{O_{X_η}} O𝔹_dR))^{∇=0}. If moreover L is a Ẑ_p-local system (torsionfree), it is a de Rham local system.

items.name: filtration condition via 𝔹_dR
items.statement: In the setup of Definition 2.31(ii) (with (E, φ, Fil^•E) a filtered F-isocrystal), the 𝔹_{crys,K}-linear isomorphism ϑ ⊗_{K_0} K is filtered if and only if the 𝔹_dR-linear isomorphism ϑ ⊗_{𝔹_crys} 𝔹_dR : 𝔹_dR(E) ≅ 𝔹_dR ⊗_{Ẑ_p} L is filtered.

items.name: crystallinity can be tested on a universal cover
items.statement: Any connected framed open U ⊂ X has a V_0-model Ũ = Spf(R^+) (Lemma 2.9); the p-completed normalization of R^+ in the maximal étale extension of R = R^+[1/p] gives a perfectoid cover (R,R^+) → (S,S^+) of Ũ_η with Galois group G_{Ũ_η}. To make L crystalline it suffices to give isomorphisms E(𝔹_crys(S,S^+)) ≅ 𝔹_crys(S,S^+) ⊗_{Z_p} L(Spa(S,S^+)), compatible in U, preserving the G_{Ũ_η}-action, Frobenius, and filtrations after ⊗_{K_0}K.

items.name: crystalline local systems embed fully faithfully into filtered F-isocrystals
items.statement: Let X be a quasi-compact smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K and L_1, L_2 crystalline sheaves of Ẑ_p-modules with associated filtered F-isocrystals (E_i, φ_i, Fil^•(E_i)). The natural map Hom(L_1,L_2) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p → Hom_{fVect^φ(X_η,𝔹_crys)}(𝔹_crys ⊗ L_1, 𝔹_crys ⊗ L_2) ≅ Hom_{fIsoc^φ(X_s/V_0)}(E_1, E_2) is an isomorphism; in particular the functor from crystalline sheaves (up to isogeny) to filtered F-isocrystals is fully faithful.
items.note: Quasi-compactness added (sourceIssues E10); the exact sequence in the proof has its quotient reversed (sourceIssues E11).

items.name: auxiliary pd-thickenings O𝔸_crys(0), O𝔸_crys(1), D^+(1) and their de Rham analogues
items.statement: For an affine open Spf(R) ⊂ X and U ∈ Perfd/Spf(R)_{η,proét} with Û = Spa(S,S^+): O𝔸_crys(0)(S,S^+), O𝔸_crys(1)(S,S^+), D^+(1) are the p-completed pd-envelopes of (R ⊗_W 𝔸_inf(S,S^+))^∧_p → S^+, (R ⊗_W R ⊗_W 𝔸_inf(S,S^+))^∧_p → S^+ and (R ⊗_W R)^∧_p → R (ad hoc, different from [TT19]); they form a diagram of pro-pd-thickenings in (X_{p=0}/V_0)_conv with maps p_1,p_2 : R ⇉ D^+(1), q_1,q_2 : O𝔸_crys(0) ⇉ O𝔸_crys(1), 𝔸_crys(S,S^+) → O𝔸_crys(0). After inverting p it maps (Frobenius-twisted) to the diagram of infinitesimal thickenings D(1), O𝔹^+_dR(1)(S,S^+), R[1/p], O𝔹^+_dR(S,S^+), 𝔹^+_dR(S,S^+) (u : 𝔹^+_dR → O𝔹^+_dR), where D(1), O𝔹^+_dR(1) are the formal completions of D^+(1)[1/p] → R[1/p] and φ^*O𝔸_crys(1)[1/p] → S, using (φ^*O𝔸_crys(0)[1/p])^∧_{ker θ̃} ≃ ((R ⊗_W 𝔸_inf)^∧_p[1/p])^∧_{ker θ̃} ≃ O𝔹^+_dR(S,S^+).

items.name: E ⊗ O𝔹_dR with product connection = 𝔹_dR(E) ⊗ O𝔹_dR
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K, E a convergent isocrystal on (X_{p=0}/V_0)_conv with underlying (E, ∇_E) (Proposition 2.17), ∇_{O𝔹_dR} the connection of O𝔹_dR, and ∇' the product connection on E ⊗_{O_{X_η}} O𝔹_dR. Then (E ⊗_{O_{X_η}} O𝔹_dR, ∇') is naturally isomorphic to (𝔹_dR(E) ⊗_{𝔹_dR} O𝔹_dR, id ⊗ ∇_{O𝔹_dR}).

items.name: compatibility of filtrations on E ⊗ O𝔹_dR
items.statement: If moreover E underlies a filtered isocrystal (E, Fil^•(E)) and Fil^•𝔹_dR(E) is the filtration of Construction 2.28, then the product filtration Fil^•E ⊗_{O_{X_η}} Fil^•O𝔹_dR is naturally isomorphic to Fil^•𝔹_dR(E) ⊗_{Fil^•𝔹_dR} Fil^•O𝔹_dR.

items.name: 𝔹_dR(E) as horizontal sections
items.statement: Consequence of Proposition 2.36: 𝔹_dR(E) = (E ⊗_{O_{X_η}} O𝔹_dR)^{∇'=0}, and this identification is filtered when E underlies a filtered isocrystal.

items.name: crystalline implies de Rham
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K and L a Ẑ_p-lisse sheaf on X_η. If L is crystalline (Definition 2.31) with associated filtered F-isocrystal (E, φ, Fil^•E), then L is de Rham (Definition 2.5) with associated filtered vector bundle with flat connection (E, ∇, Fil^•E).

items.name: weakly crystalline implies crystalline
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K. Every weakly crystalline lisse sheaf L on X_{η,proét} is crystalline for a uniquely determined filtration on the associated F-isocrystal (namely Fil^•E := ν_*(Fil^•O𝔹_dR ⊗_{Ẑ_p} L), ν : X_{η,proét} → X_{η,ét}).

items.name: Liu–Zhu: de Rham criterion and Riemann–Hilbert
items.statement: For a Z_p-local system L on a smooth rigid space X_η over K: if ν_*(L ⊗ O𝔹_dR) has the same rank as L[1/p] then L[1/p] is de Rham; for de Rham L, E = ν_*(L ⊗ O𝔹_dR) with Fil^•E = ν_*(Fil^•(L ⊗ O𝔹_dR)) is a filtered vector bundle with integrable connection satisfying Griffiths transversality, and L ⊗ O𝔹_dR ≅ E ⊗ O𝔹_dR as filtered modules with connection.

items.name: Drinfeld–Mathew descent for analytic vector bundles
items.statement: Vector bundles on Spec(A) ∖ V(p, I), as (A,I) ranges over prisms (or over the generic fibre of p-complete rings), satisfy descent for (p,I)-completely faithfully flat maps.

items.name: analytic prismatic crystals Vect^an(X_Δ)
items.statement: For X a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme over O_K: Vect^an(X_Δ) := lim_{(A,I)∈X_Δ} Vect(Spec(A) \ V(p, I)), the category of analytic prismatic crystals (in vector bundles).

items.name: analytic crystals via the quasi-syntomic site
items.statement: Let X be a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme over O_K. Define Vect^an(X_qrsp, Δ_•) := lim_{S∈X_qrsp} Vect(Spec(Δ_S) \ V(p, I)). Then there is a natural equivalence Vect^an(X_Δ) ≃ Vect^an(X_qrsp, Δ_•), and a similar equivalence for the derived (∞-)categories of perfect complexes on the analytic loci. (The proof shows that S ↦ Vect(Spec(Δ_S) \ V(p, I)) is a sheaf of categories on X_qrsp for the quasi-syntomic topology.)

items.name: Frobenius preserves the analytic locus
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism with Frobenius φ. Then φ induces natural endomorphisms of the closed subscheme V(p, I) ⊂ Spec(A) and of its complement Spec(A) \ V(p, I). (Proof given: φ(d) = d^p + pδ(d) ∈ (p, d) for d ∈ I, so (p, φ(I)) ⊆ (p, I); for the complement one also needs I ⊆ √(p, φ(I)), which follows from d^p = φ(d) − pδ(d).)

items.name: F-vector bundles on the analytic locus of a prism
items.statement: Let (A, I) be a prism and U = Spec(A) \ V(p, I). The category Vect^φ(U) has objects pairs (M, φ_M) with M a vector bundle on U and φ_M : φ_A^*M[1/I] → M[1/I] an A-linear isomorphism (φ_A^*M is a vector bundle on U by Lemma 3.4); morphisms are maps of vector bundles compatible with the φ_M.

items.name: analytic prismatic F-crystals Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ)
items.statement: For a p-adic formal scheme X over O_K: Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) := lim_{(A,I)∈X_Δ} Vect^φ(Spec(A) \ V(p, I)), the category of analytic prismatic F-crystals over X.

items.name: analytic F-crystals via the quasi-syntomic site
items.statement: Let X be a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme over O_K. Define Vect^{an,φ}(X_qrsp) := lim_{S∈X_qrsp} Vect^φ(Spec(Δ_S) \ V(p, I)). There is a natural equivalence Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) ≃ Vect^{an,φ}(X_qrsp, Δ_•); ditto for derived (∞-)categories of perfect complexes. (The proof shows (A, I) ↦ Vect^φ(Spec(A) \ V(p, I)) is a sheaf of categories on X_Δ for the (p, I)-completely flat topology.)

items.name: Proposition 3.7: restriction to the analytic locus is fully faithful
items.statement: Let X be a quasi-syntomic p-adic formal scheme over O_K which is flat over O_K (e.g. X smooth over O_K). The restriction functor Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) is fully faithful.
items.note: Printed under the standing hypothesis 'quasi-syntomic over O_K' only; false for X = Spec k (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: analytic = ordinary prismatic F-crystals over O_K
items.statement: The restriction functor Vect^φ(Spf(O_K)_Δ, O_Δ) → Vect^{an,φ}(Spf(O_K)_Δ) is an equivalence of categories.

items.name: étale realization functor T
items.statement: For X as in §3: T : Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) → Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p) ≃ Loc_{Z_p}(X_η), (E, φ_E) ↦ E ⊗_{O_Δ} O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p, induced by the open immersions Spec(A[1/I]) ⊂ Spec(A) \ V(p, I) and the equivalence of [BS23, Cor. 3.8, Ex. 4.4]. The étale realization of [BS23, Constr. 4.8] on Vect^φ(X_Δ, O_Δ) factors through T (via Prop. 3.7's restriction).

items.name: rational crystalline realization D_crys
items.statement: D_crys : Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) → Vect^{an,φ}(X_{p=0,Δ}) ≃ Isoc^φ(X_{p=0,crys}) ≃ Isoc^φ(X_{s,crys}), the composite of pullback along X_{p=0} → X, the prismatic–crystalline equivalence of Theorem 6.4(i), and restriction to the reduced special fiber (Remark 2.15). Concretely, for S quasiregular semiperfect over X_{p=0} and (A, I) = (Δ_S ≅ A_crys(S), I) (= (A_crys(S), (p))), the value of D_crys(E, φ_E) at the p-completed pd-thickening (A_crys(S), S/p) is (E_A, φ_{E_A}).

items.name: pro-étale sheaves 𝔸_inf(E)[1/μ] and 𝔸_inf(E)[1/I]^∧_p; equation (8)
items.statement: For an analytic prismatic crystal E over X_Δ (X smooth over O_K), 𝔸_inf(E)[1/μ] is the pro-étale sheaf on X_{η,proét} with 𝔸_inf(E)[1/μ](Spa(S, S^+)) := E(Δ_{S^+}, I)[1/μ] for affinoid perfectoid Spa(S, S^+) ∈ Perfd/X_{η,C,proét} (μ = [ε] − 1; note D(μ) ⊂ Spec A_inf(S^+) \ V(p, ξ̃)); p-completing gives 𝔸_inf(E)[1/I]^∧_p. Sheaf property as in Lemma 2.26. For E ∈ Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ), the étale realization satisfies (8): T(E) ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔸_inf[1/I]^∧_p ≃ 𝔸_inf(E)[1/I]^∧_p (Frobenius-equivariant).

items.name: analytic prismatic F-crystals give crystalline local systems
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K. For any E ∈ Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ), the étale realization T(E) is a crystalline Ẑ_p-local system on X_{η,proét} in the sense of Definition 2.31 (Faltings); the associated F-isocrystal is the restriction to (X_s/V_0)_crys of D_crys(E), with a Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism T(E) ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_crys ≃ 𝔸_inf(E)[1/μ] ⊗_{𝔸_inf[1/μ]} 𝔹_crys ≃ 𝔹_crys(E_s).

items.name: descent of the étale comparison to A_inf[1/μ]
items.statement: Setting: X smooth over O_K, E an analytic prismatic F-crystal with étale realization T(E) (the proof only uses the value of E on the perfect prism of S^+, so it applies to any E ∈ Vect^φ(Spec A_inf(S^+) \ V(p, ξ̃)), as used in Constr. 4.2 and Prop. 4.20). Let (S, S^+) be an affinoid perfectoid C-algebra in X_{η,proét} such that T(E)|_{Spa(S,S^+)} is trivial. Then there is a natural isomorphism of A_inf(S^+)[1/μ]-modules T(E) ⊗_{Z_p} A_inf(S^+)[1/μ] ≃ 𝔸_inf(E)[1/μ](S, S^+) = E(Δ_{S^+})[1/μ], functorial in such (S, S^+), and compatible with (8) after base change along A_inf(S^+)[1/μ] → A_inf(S^+)[1/ξ̃]^∧_p (hence Frobenius-equivariant).

items.name: naturality of the realizations
items.statement: For a morphism f : E_1 → E_2 in Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) (X smooth over O_K) and Spa(S, S^+) ∈ Perfd/X_{η,C,proét} trivializing T(E_i), the isomorphisms T(E_i) ⊗ B_crys(S^+) = E_i(A_inf(S^+), I) ⊗ B_crys(S^+) ≃ E_{i,crys}(A_crys(S^+), S^+/p)[1/μ] are compatible with f; after sheafifying, the crystalline comparison T(E) ⊗ 𝔹_crys ≃ 𝔸_inf(E)[1/μ] ⊗ 𝔹_crys ≃ 𝔹_crys(E_s) is natural in E. With Cor. 2.30 and Cor. 2.35 this gives a commutative diagram relating Hom_{Vect^{an,φ}}(E_1, E_2) to Hom_{Loc_{Z_p}}(T(E_1), T(E_2)) ⊗ Q_p ≃ Hom_{fVect^φ(X_η,𝔹_crys)}(…) ≃ Hom_{fIsoc^φ(X_s/V_0)}(E_{s,1}, E_{s,2}) via T(−) and D_crys(−).

items.name: faithfulness of the étale realization
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K and f : E → E′ a morphism of analytic prismatic crystals on X (Definition 3.1). If the base change f ⊗ id : E ⊗_{O_Δ} O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p → E′ ⊗_{O_Δ} O_Δ[1/I_Δ]^∧_p is 0, then f = 0. In particular the étale realization T of Construction 3.9(i) is faithful.

items.name: lattice realization Φ
items.statement: Let S be a p-torsionfree perfectoid O_C-algebra, Y = Spf S, U = Spec(Δ_S) ∖ V(p, I). The lattice realization Φ : Vect^φ(U) → {(M, Ξ) : M ∈ Loc_{Z_p}(Y_η), Ξ ⊂ M ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_dR a 𝔹⁺_dR-lattice} sends (E, φ) to M = T(E) and to Ξ := φ*(E) ⊗ 𝔹⁺_dR = 𝔸_inf(E) ⊗_{𝔸_inf, φ} 𝔹⁺_dR ⊂ M ⊗ 𝔹_dR, using the isomorphism M ⊗ 𝔹_dR ≅ 𝔸_inf(E)[1/μ] ⊗_{𝔸_inf, φ} 𝔹_dR obtained by base change from Lemma 3.13. Morphisms (M, Ξ) → (M′, Ξ′) are maps of local systems g with (g ⊗ id)(Ξ) ⊆ Ξ′.
items.note: Printed with 𝔸_inf(E)[1/μ] in the definition of Ξ, which gives the whole 𝔹_dR-module (sourceIssues E13).

items.name: intersection formula over Δ_S (integral case)
items.statement: Let V_0⟨T_i^{±1}⟩ → R_0 be a V_0-framing of a smooth p-adic O_K-algebra R = R_0 ⊗_{V_0} O_K (Lemma 2.9; V_0 = W(k)), R_∞ := (V_0⟨T_i^{±1/p^∞}⟩ ⊗_{V_0⟨T_i^{±1}⟩} R)^∧_p, and S := (R_∞ ⊗_{O_K} O_C)^∧_p (an integral perfectoid O_C-algebra). With ξ_r := μ/φ^{−r}(μ) = ξ φ^{−1}(ξ) ⋯ φ^{−r+1}(ξ): ⋂_r (μ/φ^{−r}(μ)) Δ_S = μ Δ_S.

items.name: intersection formula after inverting p or I
items.statement: With R, S as in Lemma 4.3: ⋂_r (μ/φ^{−r}(μ)) Δ_S[1/p] = μ Δ_S[1/p] and ⋂_r (μ/φ^{−r}(μ)) Δ_S[1/I] = μ Δ_S[1/I].

items.name: lattice realization is fully faithful
items.statement: Let S be as in Lemma 4.3 (S = (R_∞ ⊗_{O_K} O_C)^∧_p for a framed smooth R). The lattice realization functor Φ of Construction 4.2 is fully faithful.

items.name: fullness of the étale realization
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K and (E, φ_E), (E′, φ_{E′}) ∈ Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ). Then every morphism g : T(E) → T(E′) of étale realizations equals T(f) for some morphism f : (E, φ_E) → (E′, φ_{E′}). Together with Lemma 4.1: T : Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) → Loc_{Z_p}(X_η) is fully faithful.

items.name: isogeny category Isoc^{an,φ}(X_Δ)
items.statement: Isoc^{an,φ}(X_Δ) has the objects of Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) and Hom_{Isoc^{an,φ}}(E, E′) := Hom_{Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ)}(E, E′) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p.

items.name: filtered enhancement of D_crys is fully faithful
items.statement: (X smooth over O_K.) The rational crystalline realization D_crys : Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) → Isoc^φ(X_s/V_0) naturally factors through a fully faithful functor D̃_crys : Isoc^{an,φ}(X_Δ) → fIsoc^φ(X_s/V_0) to filtered F-isocrystals.

items.name: canonical associated F-isocrystal of T(E)
items.statement: For any E ∈ Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) (X smooth over O_K), the filtered F-isocrystal associated with the crystalline local system T(E) is canonically the filtered enhancement D̃_crys(E) of D_crys(E), unique up to unique isomorphism.

items.name: essential surjectivity of the étale realization
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K and T a Ẑ_p-crystalline local system over X_η (Definition 2.31). Then there is a natural analytic prismatic F-crystal in Vect^{an,φ}(X_qrsp) (≃ Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) by Lemma 3.6) whose étale realization recovers T.

items.name: the subcategory X^w_qrsp
items.statement: X^w_qrsp is the full subcategory of X_qrsp of those qrsp S for which Spf(S) → X factors as Spf(S) →f Spf(S′) →g X with f and g quasi-syntomic and S′ ∈ X_qrsp a perfectoid O_C-algebra such that the restriction T|_{Spf(S′)_η} of every Ẑ_p-local system T on X_{η,proét} is trivial.

items.name: X^w_qrsp is a basis
items.statement: (X smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K.) The subcategory X^w_qrsp forms a basis of the quasi-syntomic site X_qrsp. More precisely, for X = Spf(R) affine and connected, the p-completion S of an absolute integral closure of the domain R is a perfectoid O_C-algebra, R → S is a quasi-syntomic (p-completely faithfully flat) cover, and every Ẑ_p-local system on X_{η,proét} becomes trivial on Spf(S)_η; for any qrsp cover R → R′, S ⊗̂_R R′ ∈ X^w_qrsp covers R′.

items.name: F-crystal M′ over Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p] attached to a filtered F-isocrystal
items.statement: (X smooth over O_K.) Given a filtered F-isocrystal (E, φ_E, Fil^•(E)) over X_s (Definition 2.18): M_1(S) := E(A_crys(S))[1/p] with Frobenius φ_{M_1} : φ*M_1 ≅ M_1 (a sheaf of finite projective Δ_•{I/p}[1/p]-modules); M_2 := M_1 ⊗_{Δ_•{I/p}[1/p], φ̃} Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p] with base-changed Frobenius; the B_dR-bundle M_2 ⊗ B_dR carries the tensor-product filtration Fil^•E(R[1/p]) ⊗_s (I^•·Δ_S[1/p]^∧_I) defined locally via a lift s (Construction 2.28); M′ is obtained from M_2 by Beauville–Laszlo modification at V(I_Δ) by Fil^0(M_2 ⊗ B_dR), with φ_{M′} := φ_{M_2}[1/I] (using that φ(I) is invertible in Δ_•⟨I/p⟩[1/p]).

items.name: M′ recovers the isocrystal on the crystalline locus
items.statement: Let (E, φ_E, Fil^•(E)) be a filtered F-isocrystal over X_s (X smooth over O_K). The F-crystal (M′, φ_{M′}) over (X_qrsp, Δ_•⟨I_Δ/p⟩[1/p]) satisfies: for S ∈ X_qrsp there are natural isomorphisms of finite projective F-modules over B^+_crys(S) = Δ_S{I/p}[1/p]: E(A_crys(S))[1/p] ≃ M′(S) ⊗_{Δ_S⟨I/p⟩[1/p]} Δ_S{I/p}[1/p].

items.name: M′ is the étale lattice at the Hodge–Tate divisor
items.statement: Assume moreover that (E, φ_E, Fil^•(E)) is associated with a Ẑ_p-crystalline local system T (Definition 2.31). Then for a perfectoid S ∈ X_qrsp (the proof takes S ∈ X^w_qrsp), the completed localization of M′(S) along V(I) is naturally isomorphic to (T ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹^+_dR)(S[1/p]).

items.name: crystalline comparison on X^w_qrsp
items.statement: Let T be a Ẑ_p-crystalline local system on X_η with associated filtered F-isocrystal (E, φ_E, Fil^•(E)), and S ∈ X^w_qrsp. There is a natural Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism of Δ_{S,perf}{I/p}[1/μ]-modules T(S[1/p]) ⊗_{Ẑ_p(S[1/p])} Δ_{S,perf}{I/p}[1/μ] ≃ E(Δ_{S,perf}{I/p})[1/μ]; base change along φ̃ : Δ_{•,perf}{I/p}[1/μ] → Δ_{•,perf}{φ(I)/p}[1/φ(μ)] → Δ_{•,perf}⟨I/p⟩[1/φ(μ)] gives an equivariant isomorphism T(S[1/p]) ⊗ Δ_{S,perf}⟨I/p⟩[1/φ(μ)] ≃ E(Δ_{S,perf}{I/p}) ⊗_{φ̃} Δ_{S,perf}⟨I/p⟩[1/φ(μ)].

items.name: the adic space Y and its annuli Y_[a,b]
items.statement: For S ∈ X^w_qrsp: Y := Spa(Δ_{S,perf}, Δ_{S,perf}) \ V(p, I), an analytic adic space over Spa(A_inf, A_inf) \ V(p, I). Fix p^♭ = (p, p^{1/p}, …) ∈ O_{C^♭}. For rationals 0 ≤ a = r_1/s_1 ≤ b = r_2/s_2 ≤ ∞: Y_[a,b] := {x ∈ Y : |[p^♭](x)|^{s_1} ≤ |p(x)|^{r_1}, |p(x)|^{r_2} ≤ |[p^♭](x)|^{s_2}} and Y_[a,∞) := {x : |[p^♭](x)|^{s_1} ≤ |p(x)|^{r_1}, [p^♭](x) ≠ 0}; each Y_[a,b] is a rational (hence affinoid, [Hub94, Prop. 1.3]) subspace. B_[1/p,∞] := O(Y_[1/p,∞]) = Δ_{S,perf}⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ≃ Δ_{S,perf}⟨[p^♭]^p/p⟩[1/p]. Y° := Y_[1/p,∞) \ V(μ) = Y_[1/p,∞) \ ⋃_{n>0} V(φ^{−n}(I)) (the equality V(μ) = ⋃_{n>0} V(φ^{−n}(I)) on Y_[0,∞) via [BMS18, Lem. 3.23]).

items.name: local construction of M_S on X^w_qrsp and its functoriality
items.statement: (X smooth over O_K, T a Ẑ_p-crystalline local system on X_η with filtered F-isocrystal (E, φ_E, Fil^•E).) One can associate with each S ∈ X^w_qrsp an analytic prismatic F-crystal M_S ∈ Vect^φ(Spec(Δ_{S,perf}) \ V(p, I)) such that S ↦ M_S is functorial: for every arrow f : S_1 → S_2 in X^w_qrsp there is an isomorphism of vector bundles β_f : f^*M_{S_1} → M_{S_2} over Spec(Δ_{S_2,perf}) \ V(p, I), satisfying the cocycle condition for compositions. (Construction: glue the F-bundle M′ on Y_[1/p,∞] defined by M′(S_perf) with the F-bundle N′ on Y_[0,∞) obtained from T|_{Spf(S_perf)_η} ⊗ O_{Y_[0,∞)} by modifying at V(μ) by (M′)^∧_μ, via the Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism (12): M′(S_perf) ⊗ O_{Y°}[1/I] ≃ E(Δ_{S,perf}{I/p})[1/p] ⊗ O_{Y°}[1/I] ≃ T|_{Spf(S_perf)_η} ⊗_{Z_p} O_{Y°}[1/I]; then algebraize by [Ked20, Thm. 3.8].)

items.name: compatibility of M_S with M′
items.statement: In the setting of Theorem 4.15(i), there is a natural isomorphism, for S ∈ X^w_qrsp, M_S⟨I/p⟩[1/p] ≃ M′(S) ⊗_{Δ_S} Δ_{S,perf} (M′ from Proposition 4.11), compatible with the isomorphisms β_f of (i).

items.name: étale realization of M_S
items.statement: For each perfectoid S ∈ X^w_qrsp, completing the construction of Theorem 4.15 at V(p) gives (M_S ⊗_{O_Y} O_Y[1/I])^∧_p = (T ⊗ O_Y[1/I])^∧_p = T ⊗ Δ_S[1/I]^∧_p; hence (by [BS23, Cor. 3.8] and Theorem 4.15(i)) the étale realization of the descended object is the original crystalline local system T.

items.name: Frobenius invariants on the self-product prism
items.statement: Let X = Spf(R) be a smooth p-adic formal O_K-scheme, S a perfectoid O_C-algebra in X^w_qrsp, S′ := S ⊗̂_R S, and q_1, q_2 ∈ Δ_{S′} the images of q = [ε] ∈ Δ_{O_C} under the two maps O_C → S ⇉ S′. For all n ∈ N the natural maps Δ_{S′}[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))]^{φ=1} → Δ_{S′}⟨φ^n(I)/p⟩[1/(p(q_1−1)(q_2−1))]^{φ=1} are isomorphisms on cohomology in degree 0.

items.name: invertibility of (q_1−1)(q_2−1)
items.statement: Same setting: (q_1 − 1)(q_2 − 1) is invertible in Δ_{S′}⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩[1/p].

items.name: Mayer–Vietoris sequence for Δ_{S′}
items.statement: Same setting: the natural ring maps give a short exact sequence 0 → Δ_{S′} → Δ_{S′}⟨(q_1−1)^p/p⟩ ⊕ Δ_{S′}⟨p/(q_1−1)^p⟩ → Δ_{S′}⟨p/(q_1−1)^p, (q_1−1)^p/p⟩ → 0.

items.name: boundedness of descent data at the boundary
items.statement: Assume X = Spf(R) is affine (smooth) over O_K. Let S be a perfectoid O_C-algebra covering X, and M ∈ Vect^φ(Spec(Δ_S) \ V(I, p)) an analytic prismatic F-crystal on S whose étale realization T(M) is trivializable. Assume M⟨I/p⟩[1/p] descends to Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•⟨I_Δ/p⟩[1/p]). Then M[1/p] descends to Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•[1/p]).

items.name: functoriality of the descent
items.statement: Let f : S_1 → S_2 be a map of perfectoid rings in X^w_qrsp and M_i ∈ Vect^φ(Spec(Δ_{S_i}) \ V(I, p)) with a pullback isomorphism β_f : f^*M_1 ≅ M_2, such that both M_i⟨I/p⟩[1/p] descend to the same object of Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•⟨I_Δ/p⟩[1/p]) and its evaluations at R → S_1 and R → S_1 → S_2 are compatible with β_f⟨I/p⟩[1/p]. Then the descents of M_1[1/p] and M_2[1/p] from (i) are the same object and its evaluation maps are compatible with β_f[1/p].

items.name: descent of M_S[1/p]
items.statement: Assume X = Spf(R) is affine (smooth) over O_K and let S ∈ X^w_qrsp cover X. Then the p-inverted F-crystal M_S[1/p] (over Δ_{S,perf}[1/p]; printed as an object of Vect^φ(Spec(Δ_{S,perf}) \ V(p, I))) from Theorem 4.15 descends to a prismatic F-crystal M̃[1/p] ∈ Vect^φ(X_qrsp, Δ_•[1/p]), independent of the choice of S ∈ X^w_qrsp.

items.name: Kedlaya: algebraicity of vector bundles on punctured spectra of Witt rings
items.statement: For a perfectoid (or suitable perfect) ring R⁺ with pseudouniformizer, vector bundles on the adic space Spa(W(R⁺), W(R⁺)) ∖ V(p, [ϖ]) are equivalent to vector bundles on the scheme Spec W(R⁺) ∖ V(p, [ϖ]); φ-modules of this kind over products of valuation rings are free (Ivanov), and finitely presented φ-modules over suitable perfect rings are projective (Kedlaya–Liu).
items.locator: Remark 1.5, p. 4; proof of Theorem 4.15, p. 43; Proposition 9.9, p. 86, citing [Ked20, Thm 3.8], [Iva23, Thm 6.1], [KL15, Prop. 4.?]

items.name: Rational subsets of adic spectra are affinoid
items.statement: For a Huber pair (A, A⁺), rational subsets of Spa(A,A⁺) are affinoid (with the rational localization).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 4.15, p. 44, citing [Hub94, Prop. 1.3]

items.name: Absolute integral closures in mixed characteristic
items.statement: For a p-complete regular (or excellent) ring R, the p-completed absolute integral closure R⁺^∧ is perfectoid, and for R regular R⁺ is flat over R (Bhatt).
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 4.10, p. 40, citing [Bha20, Lem. 4.?, Thm 4.?]

items.name: Quasi-syntomic base change and flatness facts
items.statement: Quasi-syntomic maps are stable under base change; qrsp rings push out along quasi-syntomic covers; p-completely flat algebras over p-torsionfree rings are p-torsionfree.

items.name: The (p-complete) arc-topology
items.statement: arc-covers of (p-complete) rings, detected on rank ≤ 1 valuation rings; arc-local rings.

items.name: arc_p-descent for étale cohomology of generic fibres
items.statement: S ↦ RΓ_ét(Spec S[1/p], F) (F torsion) satisfies arc_p-descent on p-complete rings; comparison with RΓ_ét(Spa(S[1/p]), F) for p-complete S (Scholze).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.1, pp. 55–56, citing [BM21, Cor. 6.17, Prop. 3.?], [Sch17, Lem. 15.?]

items.name: Prismatic F-crystals in perfect complexes D^φ_perf(X_Δ)
items.statement: Let X be a bounded p-adic formal scheme. For (A,I) ∈ X_Δ let D^φ_perf(A) be the ∞-category of pairs (ℰ, φ_ℰ) with ℰ a perfect A-complex and φ_ℰ : φ_A^*ℰ ⊗^L_A A[1/I] → ℰ ⊗^L_A A[1/I] an isomorphism (φ_A^* = derived pullback along the Frobenius φ_A; from §5 on all pullbacks f^* mean Lf^* and ℰ/x means ℰ ⊗^L_A A/x). A map of prisms (A,I) → (B,J) in X_Δ induces D^φ_perf(A) → D^φ_perf(B), (ℰ,φ_ℰ) ↦ (ℰ ⊗^L_A B, φ_ℰ ⊗ id_B), using (φ_A^*ℰ) ⊗^L_A A[1/I] ⊗^L_A B ≃ (φ_A^*ℰ) ⊗^L_A B[1/J] ≃ φ_B^*(ℰ ⊗^L_A B) ⊗^L_B B[1/J] (A → B is Frobenius-equivariant and IB = J). The presheaf (A,I) ↦ D^φ_perf(A) satisfies (p,I)-completely faithfully flat descent, and one defines D^φ_perf(X_Δ) = D^φ_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ) := lim_{(A,I)∈X_Δ} D^φ_perf(A) (eq. (14)); similarly D^φ_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p) := lim over (A,I) ∈ X_Δ of pairs (ℰ perfect over A[1/I]^∧_p, isomorphism φ_ℰ : φ^*ℰ ≃ ℰ).

items.name: Laurent F-crystal in perfect complexes
items.statement: (Remark 5.2) An object of D^φ_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p) is equivalently a crystal of perfect complexes ℰ ∈ D_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p) together with an isomorphism φ_ℰ : φ^*ℰ ≃ ℰ (ℐ_Δ is already invertible in 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p). Such a pair (ℰ, φ_ℰ) is called a Laurent F-crystal in perfect complexes.

items.name: Perfection 𝒪_Δ,perf and perfection ℰ_perf of a Laurent F-crystal
items.statement: Let φ : 𝒪_Δ → φ_*𝒪_Δ be the Frobenius. The perfection of 𝒪_Δ is the derived (p, ℐ_Δ)-adic completion 𝒪_Δ,perf := (colim(𝒪_Δ → Rφ_*𝒪_Δ → Rφ^2_*𝒪_Δ → ⋯))^∧. Since the prismatic topos is replete, 𝒪_Δ,perf(A,I) = A_perf (the perfection of the prism, (colim_φ A)^∧_{(p,I)}) for every (A,I) ∈ X_Δ. Base change along 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p → 𝒪_Δ,perf[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p gives a functor D^φ_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p) → D^φ_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ,perf[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p), sending a Laurent F-crystal (ℰ, φ_ℰ) to its perfection ℰ_perf := ℰ ⊗ 𝒪_Δ,perf[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p with Frobenius φ^*ℰ_perf ≃ (φ^*ℰ) ⊗ 𝒪_Δ,perf[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p → ℰ_perf given by φ_ℰ ⊗ id.

items.name: Perfect prismatic site and the morphism π
items.statement: (Remark 5.5, first part) Let X^perf_Δ ⊂ X_Δ be the full subcategory of perfect prisms. For a (p,I)-completely faithfully flat cover (A,I) → (B,J) in X_Δ with (A,I) perfect, the perfection (A,I) → (B,J)_perf is again (p,I)-completely faithfully flat (colimit of such maps). Hence the inclusion is cocontinuous and yields a morphism of topoi π : Shv(X^perf_Δ) → Shv(X_Δ) with (π_*F)(A,I) = lim_{(A,I)→(B,J) perfect} F(B,J) = F((A,I)_perf) (eq. (15)); since tensor products of perfect prisms are perfect the inclusion is also continuous and π^{-1} is restriction.

items.name: Rπ_*𝒪_Δ ≃ 𝒪_Δ,perf and ℰ_perf ≃ Rπ_*π^*ℰ
items.statement: (Remark 5.5, second part) Let X be a bounded p-adic formal scheme. (a) Rπ_*𝒪_Δ ≃ 𝒪_Δ,perf. (b) The natural map 𝒪_Δ,perf[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p → Rπ_*(𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p) is an isomorphism. Hence π upgrades to morphisms of ringed topoi (Shv(X^perf_Δ), 𝒪_Δ) → (Shv(X_Δ), 𝒪_Δ) and (Shv(X^perf_Δ), 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p) → (Shv(X_Δ), 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p). (c) For ℰ ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p): ℰ_perf = ℰ ⊗^L 𝒪_Δ,perf[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p ≃ ℰ ⊗^L Rπ_*𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p ≃ Rπ_*π^*ℰ.

items.name: Arc-site description of the perfection: ℰ_perf ≃ Rβ_*β^*ℰ
items.statement: (Remark 5.6) Let Perfd/X be the site of affinoid perfectoid p-adic formal schemes over X with the arc-topology. Via perfectoid rings ↔ perfect prisms, Shv(X^perf_Δ) is identified with sheaves on affinoid perfectoid formal schemes over X for the p-completely flat topology, 𝒪_Δ ↦ Δ_• and 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p ↦ Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p; this gives α : Shv(Perfd/X) → Shv(X^perf_Δ). The maps Δ_• → Rα_*α^{-1}Δ_• and Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p → Rα_*α^{-1}(Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p) are isomorphisms (so both are arc-sheaves with no higher cohomology), α is a morphism of ringed topoi (Shv(Perfd/X), Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p) → (Shv(X^perf_Δ), 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p) with α^*𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p ≃ Δ_•[1/I]^∧_p, and with β := π∘α one has, for ℰ ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p), ℰ_perf ≃ Rβ_*β^*ℰ.

items.name: Arc-descent for Rν_*ℰ_perf
items.statement: Let X be a (bounded) p-adic formal scheme, ν : Shv(X_Δ) → Shv(X_ét) the canonical morphism of topoi, and ℰ ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p) with perfection ℰ_perf. Then Rν_*ℰ_perf satisfies arc-descent on the category fSch/X of p-adic formal schemes over X: for every arc-hypercover α : X_• → X the natural map Rν_{X,*}ℰ_perf → R lim_{[n]∈Δ} Rν_{X_n,*} α^*_{n,Δ} ℰ_perf is an isomorphism (implicitly after pushing forward to X_ét).

items.name: Transversal prism
items.statement: A prism (A,I) is transversal if Ā = A/I is p-torsion-free.

items.name: Global sections of vector bundles on the analytic locus of a noetherian transversal prism
items.statement: Let (A,I) ∈ X_Δ be a transversal prism with A noetherian, U := Spec(A) ∖ V(p,I), j : U ↪ Spec(A). For every vector bundle ℰ on U, H^0(U, ℰ) = H^0(Spec A, j_*ℰ) is a finitely presented A-module (equivalently j_*ℰ is coherent).

items.name: Breuil–Kisin-type weakly final prism of a framed smooth affine X and its Čech nerve
items.statement: (In the proof of Theorem 5.10.) Let X = Spf R be a framed smooth affine formal scheme over 𝒪_K and X̃ = Spf R̃ its smooth model over V_0 = W(k) (Lemma 2.9), with the Frobenius lift induced by the framing. Put A := R̃⟦u⟧ with δ(u) = 0 and I := ker(A → R, u ↦ π) for a uniformizer π of 𝒪_K. Then (A,I) is a transversal prism with A regular noetherian and Ā = R, weakly final in X_Δ (covers the final object); its Čech nerve (A^•, IA^•) in X_Δ (formed as in [BS22, Prop. 3.13]) has (p,I)-completely faithfully flat transition maps, and, A being noetherian, all coface maps A^0 → A^n are faithfully flat.

items.name: Theorem 5.10: analytic prismatic F-crystals as F-crystals in perfect complexes
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over O_K. There is an essentially unique fully faithful functor Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) → D^φ_perf(X_Δ) such that, for X = Spf R framed affine and (A,I) = (R̃⟦u⟧, (E(u))) a Breuil–Kisin-type prism covering X, the value at any prism (B,J) receiving a map from (A,I) is (j_{A,*}E_A) ⊗^L_A B, where j_A : Spec(A) ∖ V(p,I) ↪ Spec(A) (j_{A,*}E_A is finitely presented over the regular ring A, hence perfect), with Frobenius induced by φ_E; the result is independent of the choice of (A,I).
items.note: Printed as 'induced by pushforward along Spec(A) ∖ V(p,I) ↪ Spec(A) for all prisms (A,I) ∈ X_Δ', which fails at crystalline prisms (sourceIssues E15).

items.name: Perfectness and tor-amplitude of relative prismatic cohomology with coefficients
items.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, X a proper smooth formal Ā-scheme of relative dimension n, and ℰ a prismatic crystal in perfect complexes over (X/A)_Δ of tor-amplitude [a,b] (the statement names (ℰ,φ_ℰ) but no Frobenius is used). Then RΓ((X/A)_Δ, ℰ) is a perfect A-complex of tor-amplitude [a, b+2n].

items.name: Hodge–Tate crystal
items.statement: (Following [BL22b]) A Hodge–Tate crystal over (X/A)_Δ is an Ō_Δ-linear prismatic crystal, Ō_Δ = 𝒪_Δ/ℐ_Δ; e.g. ℰ ⊗^L Ō_Δ for a crystal ℰ of 𝒪_Δ-modules.

items.name: Hodge–Tate cohomology of Hodge–Tate crystals via the Higgs complex
items.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, X = Spf(R) a smooth affine formal Ā-scheme, and ℰ a Hodge–Tate crystal in perfect complexes over (X/A)_Δ. Choose a bounded prism R̃ over A (a δ-lift, p-completely smooth over A) with R̃/IR̃ ≃ R and set ℰ(R) := ℰ(R̃, IR̃), a perfect R-complex. Then RΓ((X/A)_Δ, ℰ) admits a finite filtration whose i-th graded piece is ℰ(R) ⊗_{𝒪_X} Ω^i_{X/Ā}{−i}[−i] (0 ≤ i ≤ dim X); ℰ(R) and the filtration are functorial in ℰ (for the fixed lift). In particular RΓ((X/A)_Δ, ℰ) is a perfect R-complex. (Proof: the lift R̃ gives D_perf((X/A)_Δ, Ō_Δ) ≃ D_perf(B T_X{1}^♯) ≃ perfect R-complexes with a nilpotent action of S = Sym_R(T_R{1}), sending ℰ to ℰ(R); then RΓ ≃ RHom_S(R, ℰ(R)) computed by the Koszul resolution of R = S/(T_R{1}·S), whose naive filtration gives the graded pieces.)

items.name: Base change for relative prismatic cohomology with coefficients
items.statement: Let (A,I) → (B,IB) be a map of bounded prisms, X a quasi-compact quasi-separated smooth formal Ā-scheme, and ℰ ∈ D_perf((X/A)_Δ) a prismatic crystal in perfect complexes, with restriction ℰ_B ∈ D_perf((X_B̄/B)_Δ). Then the natural map RΓ((X/A)_Δ, ℰ) ⊗̂^L_A B → RΓ((X_B̄/B)_Δ, ℰ_B) is an isomorphism, where ⊗̂^L is the derived (p,I)-completed tensor product.

items.name: Pushforward of a crystal in perfect complexes along a smooth proper map is a crystal
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of p-adic formal schemes and ℰ a prismatic crystal in perfect complexes on X_Δ. Then Rf_{Δ,*}ℰ is a prismatic crystal in perfect complexes on Y_Δ (its value at (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ being RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ, ℰ)). No separate proof is written.

items.name: Frobenius pullbacks of pushforwards are crystals
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of p-adic formal schemes and ℰ ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ). Then φ_{Y_Δ}^*Rf_{Δ,*}ℰ and Rf_{Δ,*}φ_{X_Δ}^*ℰ are prismatic crystals in perfect complexes (φ_{Z_Δ} = Frobenius of the absolute prismatic site); the key point is (φ_A^*ℰ(A,I)) ⊗^L_A B ≃ φ_B^*ℰ(B,IB) for maps (A,I) → (B,IB).

items.name: Weak étale comparison with coefficients
items.statement: Let X be a bounded p-adic formal scheme and ℰ ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ, 𝒪_Δ[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p). Let μ : Shv(X_{η,proét}) → Shv(X_ét) be the nearby-cycles morphism and ν : Shv(X_Δ) → Shv(X_ét) the morphism of [BS22, Constr. 4.4]. Then there is a natural isomorphism Rμ_*T(ℰ) ≃ (Rν_*ℰ)^{φ=1} (fibre of φ − 1). The same holds for relative prismatic cohomology over a perfect prism (A,I), since X_Δ ≃ (X/A)_Δ. Equivalently (eq. (17)), for all affine Spf S → X and n ≥ 1 there are compatible natural isomorphisms RΓ((Spec S[1/p])_ét, T(ℰ)/p^n) ≃ RΓ(S, Rν_*(ℰ/p^n))^{φ=1}.

items.name: φ-invariants of Laurent F-crystals are invariant under completed perfection
items.statement: Let R be an 𝔽_p-algebra that is derived complete with respect to an element t ∈ R, and R_perf the derived t-adic completion of colim_φ R. Let (E, φ_E) ∈ D^φ_perf(R[1/t]) be a Laurent F-crystal in perfect complexes (a perfect R[1/t]-complex with φ_E : φ^*E ≃ E), and E_perf := E ⊗^L_{R[1/t]} R_perf[1/t]. Then the natural map E^{φ=1} → (E_perf)^{φ=1} of derived φ-invariants is an isomorphism.

items.name: Crystalline F-crystals in perfect complexes D^φ_perf(Z_crys)
items.statement: (In the proof of Theorem 6.4) For a scheme Z in characteristic p, D^φ_perf(Z_crys) is the ∞-category of pairs (ℰ', φ_ℰ') with ℰ' a crystal of perfect complexes on Z_crys and φ_ℰ' : F_Z^*ℰ'[1/p] ≃ ℰ'[1/p] an isomorphism (F_Z the absolute Frobenius).

items.name: Absolute crystalline comparison (i-a): prismatic vs crystalline crystals in perfect complexes
items.statement: Let Z be a quasi-syntomic scheme in characteristic p > 0. There are natural (Frobenius-compatible) equivalences of ∞-categories D_perf(Z_Δ) ≃ D_perf(Z_crys) and D^φ_perf(Z_Δ) ≃ D^φ_perf(Z_crys). For Z = Spec R with R quasiregular semiperfect both are evaluation at the initial object A_crys(R) = Δ_R; in general one uses a surjection P = 𝔽_p[x_s] ↠ R, P^0 = 𝔽_p[x_s^{1/p^∞}], P^n = (n+1)-fold tensor power of P^0 over P, the weakly initial thickening A_crys(R ⊗_P P^0) → R ⊗_P P^0 whose self-coproducts are A_crys(R ⊗_P P^n), and descent: D^{(φ)}_perf(Z_?) ≃ lim_{[n]∈Δ} D^{(φ)}_perf(A_crys(R ⊗_P P^n)).

items.name: Absolute crystalline comparison (i-b): analytic prismatic (F-)crystals vs (F-)isocrystals
items.statement: Let Z be a quasi-syntomic scheme in characteristic p > 0. There are natural equivalences Vect^{an}(Z_Δ) ≃ Isoc(Z_crys) and Vect^{an,φ}(Z_Δ) ≃ Isoc^φ(Z_crys). For R quasiregular semiperfect both sides are Vect(A_crys(R)[1/p])^{(φ=1)} (note V(p,I) = V(p) for prisms in characteristic p); the general case follows by p-completely faithfully flat descent (Isoc(Z_crys) is here tacitly the category of crystals of finite projective 𝒪_crys[1/p]-modules).

items.name: Absolute crystalline comparison (ii): cohomology
items.statement: Let Z be a quasi-syntomic scheme in characteristic p > 0, ℰ ∈ D_perf(Z_Δ) and ℰ' ∈ D_perf(Z_crys) the associated object from 6.4(i). There is a natural isomorphism RΓ(Z_Δ, ℰ) ≃ RΓ(Z_crys, ℰ'), Frobenius-equivariant when ℰ has an F-structure; it is independent of the chosen surjection P ↠ R (Zariski-locally).

items.name: Frobenius pullback under the prismatic–crystalline equivalence
items.statement: Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect ring (characteristic p), F_S its absolute Frobenius, M a perfect A_crys(S)-complex, ℰ, ℰ' the associated crystals on Spec(S)_Δ and Spec(S)_crys. Then (F^*_{Spec(S)_crys}ℰ')(A_crys(S), S) = φ^*_{A_crys(S)}M = φ^*_{Δ_S}ℰ(Δ_S, (p)). Consequently the equivalence of Theorem 6.4 carries φ^*_{Z_Δ}ℰ to F^*_{Z_crys}ℰ'.

items.name: Relative vs absolute crystalline sites over A_crys(S)
items.statement: Let S be a quasiregular semiperfect ring, A = A_crys(S) ≃ Δ_S, J = ker(A_crys(S) → S), and S' an S-algebra. The forgetful functor (S'/(A,J))_crys → S'_crys is an equivalence of sites (every p-complete p-adic PD-thickening (B,L) of S' receives a unique PD-map from (A,J) compatible with S → S' → B/L). Hence crystals (resp. (F-)isocrystals) and their cohomology on the two sites agree.

items.name: Relative vs absolute prismatic sites over Δ_S
items.statement: With S, A, J, S' as in 6.7(i), and S ↪ Ā = A/p the map from the factorization of φ_Ā, the forgetful functor ((S' ⊗_S Ā)/(A,(p)))_Δ → S'_Δ is an equivalence of sites (every bounded prism (B,(p)) over S' receives a unique map of prisms (A,(p)) → (B,(p)) compatible with S → Ā → B̄ and S → S' → B̄). Hence crystals (resp. (F-)isocrystals) and cohomology on the two sites agree.

items.name: Relative crystalline comparison γ_crys
items.statement: Let S, A = A_crys(S), J be as in Lemma 6.7, Z a quasi-syntomic scheme over S, ℰ ∈ D_perf(Z_Δ) and ℰ' ∈ D_perf(Z_crys) the associated object of Theorem 6.4(i). Then ℰ (resp. ℰ') is naturally a crystal on (Z_Ā/A)_Δ, Z_Ā := Z ×_{Spec S} Spec Ā via S ↪ Ā (resp. on (Z/(A,J))_crys), and there are natural isomorphisms γ_crys : RΓ((Z/(A,J))_crys, ℰ') ≃ RΓ(Z_crys, ℰ') ≃ RΓ(Z_Δ, ℰ) ≃ RΓ((Z_Ā/A)_Δ, ℰ), Frobenius-equivariant if ℰ has a Frobenius structure. For ℰ = 𝒪_Δ and Z = Spec R affine this recovers [BS22, Thm. 5.2] for the PD ideal J ⊂ A and ψ : A/J → A/p (Z_Ā = Spec R^{(1)}).

items.name: Alternative Čech–Alexander complexes via an enlarged framing
items.statement: (Remark 6.9, used in §10) Keep S, A, J, Z = Spec R quasi-syntomic over S. Let Σ be a finite set of units of R such that P = S[x_s^{±1}; s ∈ Σ] → R, x_s ↦ s, is surjective; P^0 = S[x_s^{±1/p^∞}], P^• the Čech nerve of P → P^0, R^• := P^• ⊗_P R. Then (A_crys(R^0), R^0) is weakly initial in (Z/(A,J))_crys ≃ Z_crys; (A_crys(R^•), R^•) and (Δ_{(R^• ⊗_S Ā)/A}, (p)) are hypercovers of (Z/(A,J))_crys and (Z_Ā/A)_Δ, and there are isomorphisms RΓ((Z/(A,J))_crys, ℰ') ≃ lim_{[n]∈Δ} ℰ'(A_crys(R^n)) → lim_{[n]∈Δ} ℰ(Δ_{(R^n ⊗_S Ā)/A}) ≃ RΓ((Z_Ā/A)_Δ, ℰ) computing γ_crys.

items.name: Finite-type Čech–Alexander complex for crystalline cohomology
items.statement: (Remark 6.10, used in §10) With the notation of Remark 6.9, let D^0 be the p-completed PD-envelope of A⟨t_s^{±1}⟩ → P → R; it is weakly initial in (Z/(A,J))_crys, its (n+1)-fold self product (D^n, R) is the PD-envelope of A⟨t_s^{±1}⟩^{⊗̂_A (n+1)} → R, and t_s ↦ [(x_s, x_s^{1/p}, …)] induces D^0 → A_crys(R^0) compatible with the maps to R. The resulting maps give compatible isomorphisms RΓ((Z/(A,J))_crys, ℰ') ≃ lim_{[n]∈Δ} ℰ'(D^n, R) and ≃ lim_{[n]∈Δ} ℰ'(A_crys(R^n), R^n), functorial in the enlarged framing and Σ.

items.name: Prismatic cohomology over A_crys(S) vs the convergent F-isocrystal Rf_{s,crys,*}ℰ'[1/p]
items.statement: Let f : X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of smooth formal schemes over 𝒪_K, ℰ ∈ D^φ_perf(X_{p=0,Δ}) and ℰ' the associated crystal in perfect complexes on X_{p=0,crys}. Let (A = A_crys(S), J) be the divided power thickening attached to a quasiregular semiperfect ring S over Y_{p=0}, and X_Ā := X ×_Y Spec(A/p), where Spec(A/p) → Spec(S) → Y is the structure map of the prism. Then there is a natural Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism of perfect A[1/p]-complexes RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ, ℰ)[1/p] ≃ (Rf_{s,crys,*}ℰ'[1/p])(A, A/J).

items.name: Theorem 6.13(i): rational crystalline pushforward is a convergent F-isocrystal
items.statement: Let f : Z_1 → Z_2 be a smooth proper map of smooth 𝒪_K/p-schemes, f_s : Z_{1,s} → Z_{2,s} the induced map of reduced special fibres, and ℰ' a crystal in perfect complexes on Z_{1,crys} underlying an F-isocrystal (ℰ'[1/p], φ_ℰ') after inverting p. Then Rf_{s,crys,*}ℰ'[1/p] underlies a (convergent) F-isocrystal in perfect complexes over Z_{2,crys}, with F-structure φ^*_{Z_2}Rf_{s,crys,*}ℰ'[1/p] ≃ Rf_{s,crys,*}(φ^*_{Z_1}ℰ'[1/p]) ≃ Rf_{s,crys,*}ℰ'[1/p] (via F_ℰ').

items.name: Theorem 6.13(ii): values at p-torsionfree PD-thickenings
items.statement: In the setting of 6.13(i), for every p-complete, p-torsion-free divided power thickening (A, A/J) ∈ Z_{2,crys}, regarding Rf_{s,crys,*}ℰ'[1/p] as a crystal of complexes on the convergent site Z_{2,conv}, there is a natural isomorphism (Rf_{s,crys,*}ℰ'[1/p])(A, A/J) ≃ RΓ((Z_{1,A/J}/A)_crys, ℰ')[1/p], where Z_{1,A/J} = Z_1 ×_{Z_2} Spec(A/J).
items.note: The cited comparison ([Shi07, Thm 2.36], [Ogu90, Thm 0.7.7]) covers enlargements of finite type; its use at A_crys(S) in Corollary 6.14 needs an extension (sourceIssues E17).

items.name: Xu: higher direct images of convergent F-isocrystals
items.statement: For f smooth proper over a noetherian base in characteristic p, Rf_{crys,*}E[1/p] of an F-isocrystal is a convergent F-isocrystal and Frobenius acts as an isogeny on it.
items.locator: Remark 1.20, p. 9; proof of Theorem 6.13, p. 60, citing [Xu19, Cor. 8.3, Thm 3.22, Thm 5.10]

items.name: Rational crystalline cohomology equals convergent cohomology
items.statement: For proper smooth morphisms and enlargements of finite type, RΓ_crys(−, E)[1/p] ≅ RΓ_conv(−, E[1/p]) (Ogus over a point; Shiho relative, for (log) F-isocrystals).
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 6.13, pp. 60–61, citing [Ogu90, Thm 0.7.7], [Shi07, Thm 2.36, Cor. 2.37]

items.name: Tian: Hodge–Tate crystals, Higgs complexes and duality
items.statement: For X smooth over Ā, the cohomology of a Hodge–Tate crystal in vector bundles is computed by a Higgs complex; Grothendieck–Serre duality for Hodge–Tate cohomology with the trace trivializing the top cohomology.
items.locator: Remark 1.14, p. 8; Propositions 5.12 and 7.9, pp. 53, 62, 67, citing [Tia23, §§5–6, Thm]

items.name: Top prismatic higher direct image is a line bundle (geometrically connected case)
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of smooth (bounded p-adic) formal 𝒪_K-schemes of relative equidimension n, and assume f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_Y. Then the top prismatic higher direct image R^{2n}f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n} (Breuil–Kisin twist {n}) is a crystal in line bundles over 𝒪_{Y_Δ}: for every prism (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ, with Ā = A/I and X_Ā = X ×_Y Spf(Ā), the A-module H^{2n}((X_Ā/A)_Δ, 𝒪_Δ{n}) is finitely presented and invertible, and for every map of prisms (A,I) → (B,IB) in Y_Δ the base change map H^{2n}((X_Ā/A)_Δ, 𝒪_Δ{n}) ⊗_A B → H^{2n}((X_B̄/B)_Δ, 𝒪_Δ{n}) is an isomorphism. (The proof shows H^{2n}((X_Ā/A)_Δ, 𝒪_Δ{n}) is free of rank 1 over A for every perfect prism (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ; its Nakayama step, H^{2n} ⊗_A Ā ≅ Ā, holds for every bounded (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ, so together with invertibility it gives freeness of rank 1 for all (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ.)

items.name: Cup product on relative prismatic cohomology
items.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, Z → Spf(Ā) a p-adic formal scheme, and E₁, E₂ prismatic F-crystals in perfect complexes on (Z/A)_Δ (the F-structure is not used). For every (B,IB) ∈ (Z/A)_Δ sheafification gives E₁(B,IB) ⊗^L E₂(B,IB) → (E₁ ⊗^L E₂)(B,IB); taking R lim over (B,IB) ∈ (Z/A)_Δ gives a natural map RΓ((Z/A)_Δ,E₁) ⊗^L_A RΓ((Z/A)_Δ,E₂) ≅ R lim E₁(B,IB) ⊗^L_A R lim E₂(B,IB) → R lim (E₁ ⊗^L E₂)(B,IB) ≅ RΓ((Z/A)_Δ, E₁ ⊗^L E₂).

items.name: Cup product map for prismatic pushforward
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of p-adic formal schemes and E₁, E₂ prismatic F-crystals in perfect complexes on X_Δ. For varying (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ the maps of Construction 7.3.(i) (with Z = X_Ā) are compatible with the base change isomorphisms of Corollary 5.15 and assemble to a natural map of prismatic crystals in perfect complexes Rf_{Δ,*}E₁ ⊗^L_{𝒪_{Y_Δ}} Rf_{Δ,*}E₂ → Rf_{Δ,*}(E₁ ⊗^L E₂), called the cup product map.

items.name: Poincaré (cup product) pairing with Breuil–Kisin twist
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of p-adic formal schemes (implicitly of relative equidimension n, so that Rf_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n} has cohomology in degrees ≤ 2n), E ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ), and E^∨ := R𝓗om_{𝒪_{X_Δ}}(E, 𝒪_{X_Δ}). The pairing is the composite Rf_{Δ,*}E ⊗^L_{𝒪_{Y_Δ}} Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n} → Rf_{Δ,*}(E ⊗^L_{𝒪_{X_Δ}} E^∨{n}) → Rf_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n} → R^{2n}f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}[−2n] of the cup product map (7.3.(ii)), Rf_{Δ,*} of the evaluation map ε_E: E ⊗^L E^∨{n} ≅ E ⊗^L R𝓗om(E, 𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}) → 𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}, and the truncation map.

items.name: Frobenius structure on the dual crystal
items.statement: Let X be a p-adic formal scheme and (E, φ_E) ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ). Endow E^∨ = R𝓗om_{𝒪_{X_Δ}}(E, 𝒪_{X_Δ}) with the F-structure φ_{E^∨}: φ^*E^∨[1/I_Δ] ≅ φ^*R𝓗om(E,𝒪_{X_Δ})[1/I_Δ] → R𝓗om(φ^*E[1/I_Δ], φ^*𝒪_{X_Δ}[1/I_Δ]) → R𝓗om(E[1/I_Δ], 𝒪_{X_Δ}[1/I_Δ]) ≅ E^∨[1/I_Δ], where the second map is an isomorphism because E is perfect and the third is ((φ_E^{−1})^∨, φ_{𝒪_{X_Δ}}), i.e. g ↦ φ_𝒪 ∘ g ∘ φ_E^{−1}. (On E^∨{n} one uses φ_{E^∨} ⊗ φ_{𝒪{n}}.)

items.name: Evaluation map is Frobenius-equivariant
items.statement: Let X be a p-adic formal scheme and E ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ), and let ε_E: E ⊗^L_{𝒪_{X_Δ}} E^∨{n} ≅ E ⊗^L R𝓗om(E, 𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}) → 𝒪_{X_Δ}{n} be the evaluation map. Then the square φ_{𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}} ∘ φ^*ε_E[1/I_Δ] = ε_E[1/I_Δ] ∘ (φ_E ⊗^L φ_{E^∨{n}}) of maps φ^*E[1/I_Δ] ⊗^L φ^*E^∨{n}[1/I_Δ] → 𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}[1/I_Δ] commutes (with the F-structure on E^∨ from Construction 7.4), with a canonical homotopy.

items.name: Frobenius structure on relative prismatic cohomology
items.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, Z → Spf(Ā) smooth and proper, and (E, φ_E) a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes on (Z/A)_Δ. For (B,IB) ∈ (Z/A)_Δ the compatibility of φ_A and φ_B gives an A-linear map φ_A^*E(B,IB) → φ_B^*E(B,IB); taking R lim gives φ_A^*RΓ((Z/A)_Δ,E) → R lim φ_A^*E(B,IB) → R lim φ_B^*E(B,IB) = RΓ((Z/A)_Δ, φ^*E). Inverting I and composing with RΓ of φ_E: φ^*E[1/I_Δ] ≅ E[1/I_Δ] gives the Frobenius structure φ_A^*RΓ((Z/A)_Δ,E)[1/I] → RΓ((Z/A)_Δ,E)[1/I].

items.name: Frobenius structure on the derived pushforward
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of p-adic formal schemes and (E, φ_E) a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes on X_Δ. The maps φ_A^*RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E)[1/I] → RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E)[1/I] of 7.6.(i), (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ, are functorial and compatible with base change, and assemble to a map of prismatic crystals in perfect complexes (21): (φ_{Y_Δ}^*Rf_{Δ,*}E)[1/I_Δ] → Rf_{Δ,*}E[1/I_Δ], the Frobenius structure on Rf_{Δ,*}E.

items.name: Cup product pairing is Frobenius-equivariant
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of p-adic formal schemes and E ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ). The pairing Rf_{Δ,*}E ⊗^L Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n} → Rf_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n} of Construction 7.3.(iii) is equivariant for the Frobenius structures of Constructions 7.4 and 7.6: the square (22) φ_{Rf_*𝒪{n}} ∘ φ^*(cup) = (cup) ∘ (φ_{Rf_*E} ⊗^L φ_{Rf_*E^∨{n}}) of maps φ^*Rf_{Δ,*}E[1/I_Δ] ⊗^L φ^*Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n}[1/I_Δ] → Rf_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}[1/I_Δ] commutes.

items.name: Trace-free Poincaré duality over a prism
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of smooth formal 𝒪_K-schemes of relative equidimension n with f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_Y, and let E be a prismatic crystal in perfect complexes on X_Δ. Let (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ be a bounded prism. Then the cup product pairing RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E) ⊗^L_A RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E^∨{n}) → RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,𝒪_Δ{n}) → H^{2n}((X_Ā/A)_Δ,𝒪_Δ{n})[−2n] induces a natural isomorphism RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E) ≅ RHom_A(RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E^∨{n}), H^{2n}((X_Ā/A)_Δ,𝒪_Δ{n})[−2n]). If E underlies a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes, the pairing and the isomorphism are Frobenius-equivariant (for the structures of Constructions 7.4, 7.6).

items.name: Trace-free Poincaré duality for the prismatic pushforward
items.statement: Same hypotheses as Theorem 7.8.(i) (f: X → Y smooth proper of smooth formal 𝒪_K-schemes, relative equidimension n, f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_Y; E a prismatic crystal in perfect complexes on X_Δ). The cup product pairing Rf_{Δ,*}E ⊗^L_{𝒪_{Y_Δ}} Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n} → Rf_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n} → R^{2n}f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}[−2n] induces a natural isomorphism Rf_{Δ,*}E ≅ R𝓗om_{𝒪_{Y_Δ}}(Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n}, R^{2n}f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}[−2n]); if E underlies a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes, pairing and isomorphism are Frobenius-equivariant.
