items.name: Local Poincaré duality for Hodge–Tate crystals (ν-pushforward)
items.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, X a smooth formal Ā-scheme of relative equidimension n, and F a Hodge–Tate crystal (𝒪̄_Δ-linear prismatic crystal; implicitly in perfect complexes) on (X/A)_Δ; let ν: Shv((X/A)_Δ) → Shv(X_ét) be the map of topoi of [BS22, Const. 4.4]. Then the cup product Rν_*F ⊗^L_{𝒪_X} Rν_*F^∨{n} → Rν_*𝒪̄_Δ{n} → R^nν_*𝒪̄_Δ{n}[−n] induces a natural isomorphism (23) Rν_*F ≅ R𝓗om_{𝒪_X}(Rν_*F^∨{n}, R^nν_*𝒪̄_Δ{n}[−n]).

items.name: Poincaré duality for cohomology of Hodge–Tate crystals (no trace choice)
items.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, X a smooth formal Ā-scheme of relative equidimension n which is proper over Spf(Ā) with H^0(X,𝒪) = Ā, and F a Hodge–Tate crystal (in perfect complexes) on (X/A)_Δ. Then the cup product RΓ((X/A)_Δ,F) ⊗^L_Ā RΓ((X/A)_Δ,F^∨{n}) → RΓ((X/A)_Δ,𝒪̄_Δ{n}) → H^{2n}((X/A)_Δ,𝒪̄_Δ{n})[−2n] induces a natural isomorphism (24) RΓ((X/A)_Δ,F) ≅ RHom_Ā(RΓ((X/A)_Δ,F^∨{n}), H^{2n}((X/A)_Δ,𝒪̄_Δ{n})[−2n]). (The identification of the constructed map with the cup-product map is left to the reader in the paper.)

items.name: Pushing forward perfect pairings along finite étale maps
items.statement: Let π: Spec(B) → Spec(A) be a finite étale morphism of affine schemes. Then a perfect pairing E₁ ⊗^L_B E₂ → B of perfect B-complexes (Definition 8.5.(i)) induces a natural perfect pairing π_*E₁ ⊗^L_A π_*E₂ → A of perfect A-complexes: the adjoint of π_*E₁ ≅ π_*RHom_B(E₂,B) ≅ π_*RHom_B(E₂,π^!A) → RHom_A(π_*E₂, π_*π^!A) → RHom_A(π_*E₂, A) (last map induced by t_{B/A}).

items.name: Prism attached to a finite étale extension of Ā
items.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism and B̄ a finite étale Ā-algebra. There is an essentially unique finite étale A-algebra B with B/IB ≅ B̄; B carries a unique δ-structure compatible with that of A; B is derived (p,I)-complete and p ∈ IB + φ(I)B. Hence (B,IB) is a (bounded) prism with a map of prisms (A,I) → (B,IB) lifting Ā → B̄.

items.name: Relative prismatic site is insensitive to finite étale base extension
items.statement: Let (A,I) be a bounded prism, and let f: Z → Spf(B̄) → Spf(Ā) be a smooth morphism of formal schemes (composite as displayed) such that B̄ is a finite étale Ā-algebra; let (B,IB) be the prism attached to the finite étale lift B of B̄. Then the forgetful functor (Z/B)_Δ → (Z/A)_Δ is an isomorphism of sites. In particular it induces an equivalence of topoi and every sheaf on (Z/A)_Δ has the same cohomology as its restriction to (Z/B)_Δ.

items.name: Non-canonical Poincaré duality for relative prismatic cohomology
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of smooth formal 𝒪_K-schemes of relative equidimension n and E ∈ D_perf(X_Δ) a prismatic crystal in perfect complexes. For each (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ there is a (non-canonical) trace map H^{2n}((X_Ā/A)_Δ,𝒪_Δ{n}) → A inducing a perfect pairing of perfect A-complexes RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E) ⊗^L_A RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E^∨{n}) → A[−2n]. (Construction: Stein factorization f = h ∘ g, X →g Y' →h Y, with g proper smooth, g_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_{Y'}, h finite étale; B̄ := Ā ⊗ 𝒪_{Y'}, with H^0(X_Ā,𝒪) = B̄; lift to (B,IB) ∈ Y'_Δ; RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E) = π_*RΓ((X_Ā/B)_Δ,E); choose a trivialization H^{2n}((X_Ā/B)_Δ,𝒪{n}) ≅ B and compose with t_{B/A}.)

items.name: Prismatic trace for a finite étale morphism
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a finite étale morphism of smooth formal 𝒪_K-schemes. For (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ put B̄ := H^0(X_Ā,𝒪) and let (A,I) → (B,IB) be its essentially unique finite étale lift. Define tr^Δ: f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}(A,I) ≅ RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,𝒪_Δ) ≅ RΓ((Spf(B̄)/A)_Δ,𝒪_Δ) ≅ B →(tr_{B/A}) A ≅ 𝒪_{Y_Δ}(A,I); these assemble to f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ} → 𝒪_{Y_Δ}.

items.name: Étale realization of the finite étale prismatic trace is the counit
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a finite étale morphism of smooth formal 𝒪_K-schemes. The standard trace for étale algebras induces a map tr^Δ: f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ} → 𝒪_{Y_Δ} whose étale realization T(tr^Δ) is identified, via Ẑ_{p,Y_η} ≅ T(𝒪_{Y_Δ}) and f_{η,*}Ẑ_{p,X_η} ≅ f_{η,*}T(𝒪_{X_Δ}) ≅ T(f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}) (Theorem 6.1), with the counit f_{η,*}Ẑ_{p,X_η} = f_{η,!}f_η^*Ẑ_{p,Y_η} → Ẑ_{p,Y_η} of the adjunction (f_{η,*} = f_{η,!}) ⊣ f_η^*.

items.name: Prismatic trace maps lifting étale trace maps
items.statement: Suppose that for every smooth proper morphism f: X → Y of smooth formal O_K-schemes of relative equidimension n a Z_p-linear map tr^ét_{f_η}: R^{2n}f_{η,*}Ẑ_{p,X_η}(n) → Ẑ_{p,Y_η} has been chosen such that (a) the collection is compatible with compositions; (b) when n = 0 it is the counit of (f_{η,*} = f_{η,!}, f_η^*); (c) it is surjective when all fibres of f are nonempty. Then there are unique Frobenius-equivariant trace maps tr^Δ_f: R^{2n}f_{Δ,*}O_{X_Δ}{n} → O_{Y_Δ} with T(tr^Δ_f) = tr^ét_{f_η}; they are compatible with compositions, are the finite étale traces when n = 0, and are isomorphisms when f_*O_X = O_Y.
items.note: Printed with 'formal O_K-schemes' (sourceIssues E23); the proof applies Proposition 7.1 outside its hypothesis f_*O_X = O_Y (sourceIssues E24).

items.name: Canonical (trace-normalized) prismatic Poincaré duality
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 7.16 (f: X → Y smooth proper of (smooth) formal 𝒪_K-schemes of relative equidimension n, trace maps chosen as there), for every prismatic crystal E in perfect complexes on X_Δ the composite (27) Rf_{Δ,*}E ⊗^L_{𝒪_{Y_Δ}} Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n} → Rf_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n} → R^{2n}f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n}[−2n] →(tr^Δ_f[−2n]) 𝒪_{Y_Δ}[−2n] is a perfect pairing, i.e. its adjoint Rf_{Δ,*}E → R𝓗om_{𝒪_{Y_Δ}}(Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n}, 𝒪_{Y_Δ}[−2n]) = (Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n})^∨[−2n] is an isomorphism. When E underlies a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes, the pairing is Frobenius-equivariant.

items.name: Prismatic traces are compatible with composition
items.statement: In Theorem 7.16, the collection {tr^Δ_f} is compatible with compositions.

items.name: Prismatic trace in relative dimension 0
items.statement: In Theorem 7.16, when n = 0 (f finite étale) tr^Δ_f is the standard trace for finite étale morphisms of algebras from Lemma 7.15.

items.name: Prismatic trace is an isomorphism for geometrically connected fibres
items.statement: In Theorem 7.16, if f_*𝒪_X = 𝒪_Y then tr^Δ_f: R^{2n}f_{Δ,*}𝒪_{X_Δ}{n} → 𝒪_{Y_Δ} is an isomorphism (R^{2n}f_{η,*}Ẑ_p(n) is then a rank-one Z_p-local system and the surjection tr^ét_{f_η} of rank-one local systems is an isomorphism).

items.name: Perfect pairing of prismatic crystals
items.statement: The pairing (27) Rf_{Δ,*}E ⊗^L Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n} → 𝒪_{Y_Δ}[−2n] is called perfect if its adjoint Rf_{Δ,*}E → R𝓗om_{𝒪_{Y_Δ}}(Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n}, 𝒪_{Y_Δ}[−2n]) = (Rf_{Δ,*}E^∨{n})^∨[−2n] is an isomorphism.

items.name: Berkovich–Zavyalov trace maps for smooth proper rigid spaces
items.statement: For f : X → Y smooth proper of rigid spaces of relative dimension n there are trace maps R^{2n}f_*Ẑ_p(n) → Ẑ_p, compatible with composition, equal to the finite étale trace in relative dimension 0, and surjective when fibres are nonempty, inducing p-adic Poincaré duality.

items.name: Frobenius isogeny for prismatic pushforward
items.statement: Let f: X → Y be a smooth proper morphism of smooth formal 𝒪_K-schemes and (E, φ_E) a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes on X_Δ. Then Rf_{Δ,*}E, with the Frobenius structure of Construction 7.6, is a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes on Y_Δ; i.e. (φ_{Y_Δ}^*Rf_{Δ,*}E)[1/I_Δ] → Rf_{Δ,*}E[1/I_Δ] is an isomorphism, equivalently for every bounded prism (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ the map φ_A^*RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E)[1/I] → RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E)[1/I] is an isomorphism of perfect A[1/I]-complexes.

items.name: Perfect pairing of perfect complexes
items.statement: Let A be a ring. A perfect pairing is a map E₁ ⊗^L_A E₂ → E₃[n] in D_perf(A) such that E₁ and E₂ are perfect A-complexes, E₃ is a locally free A-module of rank one, and the map E₂ ⊗^L_A E₃^∨[−n] → E₁^∨ induced by the adjunctions RHom_A(E₁ ⊗^L E₂, E₃) ≅ RHom_A(E₁ ⊗^L E₂ ⊗^L E₃^∨, A) ≅ RHom_A(E₂ ⊗^L E₃^∨, RHom_A(E₁,A)) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Map of perfect pairings
items.statement: A map from the perfect pairing E₁ ⊗^L_A E₂ → E₃[n] to the perfect pairing F₁ ⊗^L_A F₂ → F₃[n] is a commutative square in D_perf(A) whose left vertical arrow is α ⊗ β for given maps α: E₁ → F₁, β: E₂ → F₂, and whose right vertical arrow is a map γ: E₃[n] → F₃[n] (induced by γ: E₃ → F₃).

items.name: Maps of perfect pairings are split injections
items.statement: Let A be a ring and let (α, β, γ) be a map of perfect pairings of perfect A-complexes as in Definition 8.5.(ii), with γ: E₃ → F₃ an isomorphism. Via the isomorphisms E₂ ⊗^L E₃^∨ ≅ E₁^∨ and F₂ ⊗^L F₃^∨ ≅ F₁^∨ of Definition 8.5.(i), one has (β ⊗ (γ^∨)^{−1}[−n])^∨ ∘ α ≃ id_{E₁}. In particular α exhibits E₁ as a direct summand of F₁.

items.name: Coevaluation sends 1 to the identity
items.statement: Let E be a perfect complex over a ring A. Then the A-linear dual A → E^∨ ⊗^L_A E = RHom_A(E,E) of the canonical evaluation pairing E ⊗^L_A E^∨ → A sends 1_A to id_E ∈ H^0(RHom_A(E,E)) = Hom_{D(A)}(E,E).

items.name: Frobenius-summand lemma over a noetherian ring
items.statement: Let A be a noetherian ring, φ: A → A a faithfully flat ring endomorphism, and F ∈ D(A) a pseudo-coherent complex admitting an A-linear isomorphism F ≅ φ^*F ⊕ C in D(A). Then C = 0 and F ≅ φ^*F.

items.name: Complement of Frobenius vanishes on a Frobenius-translate locus (Breuil–Kisin prism)
items.statement: Let f: X → Y and (E, φ_E) be as in Theorem 8.1 (f smooth proper of smooth formal 𝒪_K-schemes, E a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes). Let (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ be a Breuil–Kisin prism (Footnote 10: for Y = Spf(R) framed affine with unramified model R̃, A = R̃⟦u⟧, δ(u) = 0, I = ker(A → R, u ↦ π); A regular noetherian). Assume the Frobenius structure φ_A^*RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E)[1/I] → RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E)[1/I] identifies the source with a direct summand of the target, with complement C (a perfect A[1/I]-complex). Then there is an integer n ≥ 1 such that φ^{n,*}C[1/(I·φ(I)⋯φ^{n−1}(I))] = 0.

items.name: Complement of Frobenius vanishes over rational A_crys
items.statement: Let f, E be as in Theorem 8.1, (A,I) ∈ Y_Δ a Breuil–Kisin prism, S a quasiregular semiperfect ring over Y_{p=0} with crystalline prism (A_crys(S), p) ∈ Y_Δ and a map of prisms (A, I) → (A_crys(S), (p)), and suppose φ_A^*RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E)[1/I] → RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ,E)[1/I] identifies the source with a direct summand of the target, with complement C. Then C ⊗^L_{A[1/I]} A_crys(S)[1/p] vanishes.
items.note: Printed with the base change over A[1/φ(I)] and without the map of prisms (sourceIssues E25).

items.name: Standard trace and duality for finite étale morphisms
items.statement: For finite étale f, the trace f_*O → O and the duality f_* ≅ f_! = f^! with the perfect trace pairing.

items.name: Grothendieck–Serre duality for smooth proper formal schemes
items.statement: For X smooth proper of relative dimension n over a p-complete (or I-complete) base, RΓ(X, F) and RΓ(X, F^∨ ⊗ Ω^n) are dual via the trace on H^n(X, Ω^n) (derived-completed form).

items.name: Stein factorization for flat proper maps with geometrically reduced fibres
items.statement: A flat proper finitely presented f with geometrically reduced fibres factors as X → Y′ → Y with Y′ → Y finite étale and O_{Y′} = f_*O_X.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 7.13, p. 71, citing [SP22, Tag 0G7Y]

items.name: Surjective endomorphisms of finitely generated modules are bijective
items.statement: Over a commutative ring, every surjective endomorphism of a finitely generated module is injective (Vasconcelos).
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 7.1, p. 63, citing [Vas69, Prop.]
items.note: Mathlib's OrzechProperty (Mathlib/RingTheory/OrzechProperty.lean), with its instance for commutative rings, gives this.

items.name: Associated primes of complexes and modules over noetherian rings
items.statement: Associated primes of finitely generated modules over a noetherian ring are finite and detect zero divisors and vanishing after localization.
items.locator: Proof of Lemma 8.8, p. 77, citing [SP22, Tags 00LA, 00LC, 02M3, 05BZ, 0587]
items.note: Mathlib defines associatedPrimes (Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/AssociatedPrime/Basic.lean) with finiteness over noetherian rings.

items.name: Derived Nakayama, perfectness and reflexivity of perfect complexes
items.statement: Derived Nakayama for derived I-complete complexes; perfectness and tor-amplitude can be checked modulo I; perfect complexes are reflexive; derived completion commutes with the relevant limits.
items.note: The Stacks tags 07LU and 0DJG are nilpotent-ideal statements; the paper needs their derived-complete form (a limit argument).

items.name: Local cohomology and extension of modules over punctured spectra
items.statement: Global sections of a vector bundle on Spec A agree with those on Spec A ∖ V(f,g) when (f, g) is a regular sequence ([SP22, 0G7P]); finitely presented modules on quasi-compact opens extend ([SP22, 01PI]); coherence of j_* on noetherian schemes ([SP22, 0BK1]).

items.name: Limits of 1-categories and descent data
items.statement: Homotopy limits of diagrams of 1-categories are computed by descent data.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.10, p. 51, citing [Lur09, Thm]

items.name: Pro-étale sheaf 𝔸_inf(F) attached to a prismatic crystal on Y
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of §9: K is a complete discretely valued p-adic field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k, O_K its ring of integers, C a completed algebraic closure of K; f: X → Y is a smooth proper morphism of smooth (bounded, p-adic) formal O_K-schemes. Notation: A_inf = A_inf(O_C) = W(O_C^♭); ε = (ε_i) a compatible system of p-power roots of unity in O_C^♭; q = [ε]; μ = q − 1; ξ̃ = [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1); I = the ideal generated by the image of [p]_q (the prism (A_inf, ξ̃) is identified with the initial prism Δ_{O_C}). For a prismatic crystal F (in perfect complexes) over Y_Δ, 𝔸_inf(F) is the pro-étale sheaf on Y_{η,proét} given on affinoid perfectoid Spa(S,S⁺) ∈ Perfd/Y_{η,proét} by 𝔸_inf(F)(Spa(S,S⁺)) := F(Δ_{S⁺}) (value of F on the perfect prism (A_inf(S⁺), ker θ̃) of S⁺). Claim: using the crystal condition of F and a derived version of Lemma 2.26, this is a sheaf of perfect complexes over Y_{η,proét} (cf. [Sch13, Thm. 6.5]).

items.name: Strong étale comparison
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of §9: K is a complete discretely valued p-adic field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k, O_K its ring of integers, C a completed algebraic closure of K; f: X → Y is a smooth proper morphism of smooth (bounded, p-adic) formal O_K-schemes. Notation: A_inf = A_inf(O_C) = W(O_C^♭); ε = (ε_i) a compatible system of p-power roots of unity in O_C^♭; q = [ε]; μ = q − 1; ξ̃ = [p]_q = (q^p − 1)/(q − 1); I = the ideal generated by the image of [p]_q (the prism (A_inf, ξ̃) is identified with the initial prism Δ_{O_C}). Let (ℰ, φ_ℰ) ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ) be a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes on X with étale realization T := T(ℰ) ∈ D^b_lisse(X_η, ℤ_p). Then there is a natural isomorphism of sheaves of complexes on Y_{η,C,proét} (the pro-étale site of Y_{η,C} = Y_η ×_K C, used so that μ ∈ 𝔸_inf makes sense) (Rf_{η,C,proét,*} T) ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔸_inf[1/μ] ≅ 𝔸_inf(Rf_{Δ,*} ℰ)[1/μ]. Concretely, for V = ∏_j V_j a product of p-torsionfree p-complete rank-one valuation rings over O_C with algebraically closed fraction fields (lying over Y), there is a functorial isomorphism RΓ(X_{V[1/p],proét}, T) ⊗_{ℤ_p^J} A_inf(V)[1/μ] ≅ RΓ((X_V/A_inf(V))_Δ, ℰ)[1/μ].

items.name: Rational higher direct images R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ[1/p] are vector bundles (claim in proof of Theorem 9.1)
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of §9: K is a complete discretely valued p-adic field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k, O_K its ring of integers, C a completed algebraic closure of K; f: X → Y is a smooth proper morphism of smooth (bounded, p-adic) formal O_K-schemes. Let (ℰ, φ_ℰ) ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ). For all i ∈ ℤ, R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ[1/p] is a vector bundle over (Y_Δ, 𝒪_Δ[1/p]). More precisely, let Spf R ⊆ Y be a framed affine open and (A, I) = (R̃⟦u⟧, E(u)) a Breuil–Kisin type prism (R̃ the unramified W(k)-model of R, δ(u) = 0, E(u) the Eisenstein polynomial of a uniformizer of O_K). Then (a) H^i((Rf_{Δ,*}ℰ)(A,I))[1/p] is a finite projective A[1/p]-module; and (b) (R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ)|_{(Y_Δ)/(A,I)}[1/p] ≅ H^i((Rf_{Δ,*}ℰ)(A,I))[1/p] ⊗_{A[1/p]} 𝒪_{(Y_Δ)/(A,I)}[1/p]; since such prisms cover the final object of Y_Δ this gives the claim. Intermediate assertion used: after twisting by the Breuil–Kisin twist A{−n}, n ≫ 0, the Frobenius on H^i((Rf_{Δ,*}ℰ)(A,I)){−n} is induced by a monomorphism φ_A^*H^i{−n} ↪ H^i{−n} with cokernel killed by E(u)^r, i.e. H^i{−n} is a φ-module of finite E-height.

items.name: Arc-local product setup (A = ∏ A_inf(V_j))
items.statement: Convention 9.2. Let V_j, j ∈ J, be a family of p-complete p-torsionfree valuation rings of rank one over O_C whose fraction fields are algebraically closed. Set V := ∏_{j∈J} V_j, A_j := A_inf(V_j), A := ∏_{j∈J} A_j ≅ A_inf(∏_j V_j). For i ∈ J, e_i := (δ_{ij})_{j∈J} ∈ A is the idempotent of the factor A_i. By assumption the structure map A_inf(O_C) → A is p-completely faithfully flat. The image of I = [p]_q·A in A/p = V^♭ = ∏_j V_j^♭ is again denoted I. Later notation: ι: A[1/μ] → A[1/φ(μ)] is the natural localization map.

items.name: Finitely presented modules over a product of rings
items.statement: Let A_j (j ∈ J) be any family of rings and A := ∏_{j∈J} A_j, with idempotents e_j. Let M be a finitely presented A-module and M_j := e_j·M. Then each M_j is a finitely presented A_j-module and the natural map M → ∏_{j∈J} M_j, m ↦ (e_j m)_j, is an isomorphism.

items.name: Coherence of A/p^m
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Then for every m ≥ 1 the ring A/p^m is coherent. (Generalizes [BMS18, Prop. 3.24].) In the proof: every finitely generated ideal of ∏_j V_j^♭ is principal, generated by (max{a_{1,j},…,a_{m,j}})_j (the generator of largest absolute value in each factor), and is finitely presented.

items.name: Finitely presented A-modules with M[1/p] a vector bundle are perfect
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let M be a finitely presented A-module such that M[1/p] is a vector bundle (finite projective) over A[1/p]. Then M is perfect over A.

items.name: p^∞-torsion of such modules is finitely presented
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let M be a finitely presented A-module such that M[1/p] is a vector bundle over A[1/p]. Then the submodule M[p^∞] is finitely presented (and thus perfect) over A; moreover M[p^∞] = M[p^n] for some n.

items.name: Cohomology of perfect A-complexes with locally free rationalized cohomology
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let M ∈ D_perf(A) be such that H^q(M)[1/p] is a locally free A[1/p]-module for all q ∈ ℤ. Then for all q ∈ ℤ: (i) H^q(M) is perfect as an A-complex, in particular a finitely presented A-module; (ii) H^q(M)[p^∞] ⊂ H^q(M) is perfect and thus finitely presented over A. (Parts proved simultaneously by descending induction on q.)

items.name: Injectivity into products
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. The natural maps V^♭ → V^♭[1/I] → ∏_j (V_j^♭[1/I]) and A → A[1/I]^∧_p → ∏_j (A_j[1/I]^∧_p) are injective. (In particular V^♭ is I-torsionfree and A is μ- and φ(μ)-torsionfree.)

items.name: Faithful flatness of ℤ_p^J → A and ℤ_p^J → A[1/I]^∧_p
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. The natural maps ℤ_p^J → A and ℤ_p^J → A[1/I]^∧_p are faithfully flat.

items.name: Frobenius invariants of A and A[1/I]^∧_p
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. The natural maps ℤ_p^J → fib(A --(φ − id)--> A) → fib(A[1/I]^∧_p --(φ − id)--> A[1/I]^∧_p) are isomorphisms of ℤ_p-complexes (i.e. the φ-invariants are ℤ_p^J and φ − id is surjective on A and on A[1/I]^∧_p).

items.name: Frobenius invariants of A[1/μ] → A[1/φ(μ)]
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let ι: A[1/μ] → A[1/φ(μ)] be the localization map. The natural map ℤ_p^J → fib(A[1/μ] --(φ − ι)--> A[1/φ(μ)]) is an isomorphism.

items.name: Artin–Schreier descent for perfect φ-complexes over A[1/I]^∧_p
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let N be a perfect A[1/I]^∧_p-complex with an A[1/I]^∧_p-linear isomorphism φ_N: φ^*_{A[1/I]^∧_p} N ≅ N, and let φ̃_N: N → N be its Frobenius-semilinear adjoint. Then T := fib(φ̃_N − id: N → N) is a perfect ℤ_p^J-complex and the natural φ-equivariant map T ⊗^L_{ℤ_p^J} A[1/I]^∧_p → N is an isomorphism.

items.name: Artin–Schreier descent, module case
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. In the situation of Lemma 9.8(i), assume N is concentrated in degree 0. Then T ≅ ker(φ̃_N − id: N → N) (so coker(φ̃_N − id) = 0) and the natural map T ⊗_{ℤ_p^J} A[1/I]^∧_p → N is an isomorphism.

items.name: Analytic vector bundles over the arc-local ring have free global sections
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let U := Spec(A) ∖ V(p, I) and let ℰ ∈ Vect^an(A) = Vect(U) be a vector bundle on U of constant rank r. Then H^0(U, ℰ) is a free A-module of rank r (in fact ℰ extends to a free A-module N with N|_U ≅ ℰ). (Counterpart of Lemma 5.8 for this non-noetherian A.)

items.name: Reduction of a φ-module to a free one up to bounded p-torsion
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let (M, φ_M) ∈ D^φ_perf(A) with M = H^0(M) (a module) and M[1/p] locally free of constant rank over A[1/p]. Then there exist (N, φ_N) ∈ D^φ_perf(A) and a morphism (M, φ_M) → (N, φ_N) such that N = H^0(N) is a free A-module and the kernel and cokernel of M → N are finitely presented and killed by p^n for n ≫ 0.

items.name: Finite presentation of T(M), T'(M)
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let M be a finitely presented A-module with an A-linear isomorphism φ_M: φ_A^*M[1/I] ≅ M[1/I], such that M[1/p] is locally free of finite constant rank over A[1/p] and M[p^∞] is finitely presented. Let φ̃_M: M[1/φ^{-1}(I)] → M[1/I] be the Frobenius-semilinear adjoint of φ_M. Set T'(M) := ker(φ̃_M − ι: M[1/μ] → M[1/φ(μ)]) and T(M) := ker(φ̃_M ⊗ φ_{A[1/I]^∧_p} − id: M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p → M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p). Then the ℤ_p^J-modules T(M) and T'(M) are finitely presented. (Also: T(M) ⊗_{ℤ_p^J} A[1/I]^∧_p → M[1/I]^∧_p is an isomorphism, eq. (33).)

items.name: Lattice comparison T'(M) ≅ T(M)
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let M be a finitely presented A-module with an A-linear isomorphism φ_M: φ_A^*M[1/I] ≅ M[1/I], such that M[1/p] is locally free of finite constant rank over A[1/p] and M[p^∞] is finitely presented. Let φ̃_M: M[1/φ^{-1}(I)] → M[1/I] be the Frobenius-semilinear adjoint of φ_M. Set T'(M) := ker(φ̃_M − ι: M[1/μ] → M[1/φ(μ)]) and T(M) := ker(φ̃_M ⊗ φ_{A[1/I]^∧_p} − id: M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p → M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p). Then the natural map of ℤ_p^J-modules T'(M) → T(M) is an isomorphism.

items.name: T'(M) ⊗ A[1/μ] ≅ M[1/μ]
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let M be a finitely presented A-module with an A-linear isomorphism φ_M: φ_A^*M[1/I] ≅ M[1/I], such that M[1/p] is locally free of finite constant rank over A[1/p] and M[p^∞] is finitely presented. Let φ̃_M: M[1/φ^{-1}(I)] → M[1/I] be the Frobenius-semilinear adjoint of φ_M. Set T'(M) := ker(φ̃_M − ι: M[1/μ] → M[1/φ(μ)]) and T(M) := ker(φ̃_M ⊗ φ_{A[1/I]^∧_p} − id: M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p → M ⊗_A A[1/I]^∧_p). Then the natural map of A[1/μ]-modules T'(M) ⊗_{ℤ_p^J} A[1/μ] → M[1/μ] is an isomorphism.

items.name: Derived strong étale comparison over the arc-local ring: T' ⊗ A[1/μ] ≅ M[1/μ]
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let (M, φ_M) ∈ D^φ_perf(A) with H^q(M)[1/p] locally free of constant rank over A[1/p] for all q. Let φ̃_M: M[1/φ^{-1}(I)] → M[1/I] be the semilinear adjoint of φ_M. Set T' := fib(φ̃_M − ι: M[1/μ] → M[1/φ(μ)]) and T := fib(φ̃_M ⊗ φ_{A[1/I]^∧_p} − id: M ⊗^L_A A[1/I]^∧_p → M ⊗^L_A A[1/I]^∧_p). Then the natural map of perfect A[1/μ]-complexes T' ⊗^L_{ℤ_p^J} A[1/μ] → M[1/μ] is an isomorphism.

items.name: Derived lattice comparison T' ≅ T
items.statement: A is as in Convention 9.2: A = ∏_{j∈J} A_j with A_j = A_inf(V_j), V = ∏_{j∈J} V_j, each V_j a p-complete, p-torsionfree rank-one valuation ring over O_C with algebraically closed fraction field; V^♭ = A/p = ∏ V_j^♭; I also denotes the image of [p]_q·A in V^♭. Let (M, φ_M) ∈ D^φ_perf(A) with H^q(M)[1/p] locally free of constant rank over A[1/p] for all q. Let φ̃_M: M[1/φ^{-1}(I)] → M[1/I] be the semilinear adjoint of φ_M. Set T' := fib(φ̃_M − ι: M[1/μ] → M[1/φ(μ)]) and T := fib(φ̃_M ⊗ φ_{A[1/I]^∧_p} − id: M ⊗^L_A A[1/I]^∧_p → M ⊗^L_A A[1/I]^∧_p). Then the natural map of perfect ℤ_p^J-complexes T' → T is an isomorphism.

items.name: 𝔹⁺_crys(ℰ_s), 𝔹_crys(ℰ_s) for F-isocrystals in perfect complexes
items.statement: Let X be a smooth p-adic formal scheme over Spf O_K and ℰ_s an F-isocrystal in perfect complexes over X_s. As in Definition 2.25, for U ∈ Perfd/X_{η,proét} with Û = Spa(S,S⁺) (S a perfectoid C-algebra) set 𝔹⁺_crys(ℰ_s)(U) := ℰ_s(𝔸_crys(S,S⁺), S⁺/p)[1/p] and 𝔹_crys(ℰ_s)(U) := 𝔹⁺_crys(ℰ_s)(U)[1/μ]. Claim (as in Lemma 2.26 and Remark 2.27, via the crystal property): 𝔹_crys(ℰ_s) is a sheaf of perfect complexes on X_{η,proét} equipped with a Frobenius isomorphism.
items.note: Printed text differs: (printed: '𝔸_crys(ℰ_s)(U)[1/μ]' (sourceIssues E30))

items.name: Compatibility of Definition 9.13 with Definition 2.25 on cohomology sheaves
items.statement: (Remark 9.14) For any convergent isocrystal in perfect complexes ℰ_s over X_s and any i ∈ ℤ, H^i(𝔹⁺_crys(ℰ_s)) ≅ 𝔹⁺_crys(H^i(ℰ_s)). (Stated without proof; used in the proof of Theorem B.)

items.name: Derived étale–crystalline comparison for prismatic F-crystals in perfect complexes
items.statement: Standing hypotheses of §9: K is a complete discretely valued p-adic field of characteristic 0 with perfect residue field k, O_K its ring of integers, C a completed algebraic closure of K; f: X → Y is a smooth proper morphism of smooth (bounded, p-adic) formal O_K-schemes. Let (ℰ, φ_ℰ) ∈ D^φ_perf(X_Δ) with étale realization T := T(ℰ) ∈ D^b_lisse(X_η, ℤ_p) and corresponding crystalline F-crystal ℰ' over X_{p=0,crys} (Theorem 6.4). Let ℰ_s := ℰ'[1/p]|_{X_s} be the associated F-isocrystal over (X_s/W(k))_crys. Then Rf_{s,*}ℰ_s is an F-isocrystal in perfect complexes on Y_s (Theorem 6.13(i)) and there is a natural isomorphism of sheaves of complexes on Y_{η,proét} 𝔹_crys(Rf_{s,*}ℰ_s) ≅ 𝔹_crys ⊗_{Ẑ_p} Rf_{η,*}T, compatible with the Frobenius actions on both sides. Locally, for U ∈ Perfd/Y_{η,proét} over Spa(C,O_C) with Û = Spa(S,S⁺): Rf_{s,*}ℰ_s(𝔸_crys(S,S⁺), S⁺/p)[1/p] ≅ RΓ((X_{A_crys/p}/A_crys)_Δ, ℰ)[1/p] ≅ (RΓ((X_{S⁺}/A_inf)_Δ, ℰ) ⊗^L_{A_inf} A_crys)[1/p], with A_inf = A_inf(S⁺), A_crys = A_crys(S⁺), and base change along the map of prisms (A_inf, ξ̃) → (A_crys, (p)).

items.name: Torsionfree quotient of R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ is an analytic prismatic F-crystal
items.statement: (Remark 9.16) In the setting of the proof of Theorem B (ℰ ∈ Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) with étale realization the crystalline local system L, f: X → Y smooth proper), the maximal p^∞-torsionfree quotient (R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ)_tf := R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ / (R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ)[p^∞] is an analytic prismatic F-crystal on Y with étale realization the crystalline local system (R^i f_{η,*}L)_tf. Proof sketch via Beauville–Laszlo gluing: (1) (R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ)_tf[1/p] ≅ R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ[1/p] is locally free (proof of Theorem 9.1); (2) the étale realization [BS23, Cor. 3.7] of the Laurent F-crystal (R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ)_tf[1/ℐ_Δ]^∧_p is (R^i f_{η,*}L)_tf (checked pro-étale locally using Theorem 9.1: (R^i f_{Δ,*}ℰ)_A[1/μ] ≅ R^i f_{η,*}L(S,S⁺) ⊗_{ℤ_p(S,S⁺)} A[1/μ]).

items.name: B⁺_dR-linear base changes X_{B_e} (setup of §10.1)
items.statement: Let A_{inf,K} := A_inf ⊗_{W(k)} O_K (finite A_inf-algebra). Fix a homomorphism O_K → B⁺_dR = 𝔹⁺_dR(O_C) compatible with K → C under the natural surjection B⁺_dR → C. Let θ̃_K: A_{inf,K} → O_C be induced by θ̃: A_inf → O_C and O_K → O_C. Claim: A_inf → A_{inf,K} induces an isomorphism (A_{inf,K}[1/p])^∧_{ker θ̃_K} ≅ B⁺_dR (cf. proof of Lemma 2.22). Set B⁺_{dR,e} := B⁺_dR/I^e. For a smooth morphism f: X → Y of smooth formal O_K-schemes, X_{B_e} (resp. Y_{B_e}) is the completed base change of X (resp. Y) along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_{dR,e}; for an affine open Spf(R) this is the affinoid adic space attached to (R ⊗_{O_K} A_{inf,K})^∧_p[1/p] ⊗_{A_{inf,K}} B⁺_{dR,e}. X_{B⁺} (resp. Y_{B⁺}) denotes the ind-system {X_{B_e}}_e (resp. {Y_{B_e}}_e).

items.name: Relative infinitesimal site X/Y_{B⁺_dR,inf}
items.statement: Setting of §10.1: K as before; A_inf = A_inf(O_C); B⁺_dR = 𝔹⁺_dR(O_C) = (A_inf[1/p])^∧_{ξ̃} (completion along ker θ̃, θ̃ = Hodge–Tate specialization); A_{inf,K} = A_inf ⊗_{W(k)} O_K; θ̃_K: A_{inf,K} → O_C; B⁺_{dR,e} = B⁺_dR/I^e; f: X → Y a smooth morphism of smooth formal O_K-schemes; X_{B_e}, Y_{B_e} the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_{dR,e}. The infinitesimal site X/Y_{B⁺_dR,inf} has: objects pairs (U, T) with U an open subset of the rigid space X_C and T an adic space topologically of finite type over Y_{B_e} for some e ∈ ℕ, together with a Zariski closed immersion U → T defined by a nilpotent ideal (called an infinitesimal thickening of X_C over Y_{B⁺}); morphisms (U_1,T_1) → (U_2,T_2) an open immersion U_1 → U_2 and a compatible map of adic spaces T_1 → T_2 over Y_{B_e} for some e ≫ 0; coverings families {(U_i,T_i) → (U,T)} with {T_i → T} and {U_i → U} analytic coverings. It carries the structure sheaf 𝒪_inf: (U,T) ↦ 𝒪_T(T). A crystal in vector bundles (resp. perfect complexes) assigns to each (U,T) a vector bundle (resp. perfect complex) over 𝒪_T with base-change isomorphisms for morphisms; categories Vect(X/Y_{B⁺,inf}) and D_perf(X/Y_{B⁺,inf}).

items.name: Weakly final ind-systems of thickenings
items.statement: (Remark 10.2) An ind-system {(U_i, T_i)}_i of thickenings of X_C is identified with the colimit of the associated representable sheaves; it is called weakly final if this colimit surjects onto the final object of the infinitesimal topos (compatible with the usual notion of weakly final objects).

items.name: Envelopes are weakly final
items.statement: Setting of §10.1: K as before; A_inf = A_inf(O_C); B⁺_dR = 𝔹⁺_dR(O_C) = (A_inf[1/p])^∧_{ξ̃} (completion along ker θ̃, θ̃ = Hodge–Tate specialization); A_{inf,K} = A_inf ⊗_{W(k)} O_K; θ̃_K: A_{inf,K} → O_C; B⁺_{dR,e} = B⁺_dR/I^e; f: X → Y a smooth morphism of smooth formal O_K-schemes; X_{B_e}, Y_{B_e} the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_{dR,e}. Let Z be a smooth adic space over Y_K with a closed immersion X_C → Z_C (over Y_C). Let Z_{m,e} be the m-th infinitesimal neighborhood of X_C in Z_{B_e}. Then the ind-system D_Z(X) := {Z_{m,e}}_{m,e} (the envelope of X_C in Z) is a weakly final object of X/Y_{B⁺,inf}.

items.name: Self-products of envelopes
items.statement: Setting of §10.1: K as before; A_inf = A_inf(O_C); B⁺_dR = 𝔹⁺_dR(O_C) = (A_inf[1/p])^∧_{ξ̃} (completion along ker θ̃, θ̃ = Hodge–Tate specialization); A_{inf,K} = A_inf ⊗_{W(k)} O_K; θ̃_K: A_{inf,K} → O_C; B⁺_{dR,e} = B⁺_dR/I^e; f: X → Y a smooth morphism of smooth formal O_K-schemes; X_{B_e}, Y_{B_e} the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_{dR,e}. With Z as in 10.3(i), the (n+1)-fold self product of the ind-system {Z_{m,e}}_{m,e} in the infinitesimal topos is represented by {Z^n_{m,e}}_{m,e}, where Z^n is the (n+1)-fold fibre product of Z over Y_K and Z^n_{m,e} the m-th infinitesimal neighborhood of X_C in Z^n_{B_e}.

items.name: Affine relative setup for infinitesimal cohomology
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}.

items.name: Envelope for Z = X_K (Example 10.5(1))
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}. Since X is smooth over Y, Z := X_K is smooth over Y_K and the identity gives a closed immersion X_C → Z_C. Then (as ind-systems) Z_{m,e} = X_{B_e}, and Z^n_{m,e} is the m-th infinitesimal neighborhood of X_C in (X^{×_R (n+1)})_{B_e}.

items.name: Enlarged framing and the rings D_Σ(R'), D_{Σ^n}(R') (Example 10.5(2))
items.statement: Convention 10.4 (R → R′ smooth of relative dimension d; completed base changes to B⁺_dR). An enlarged framing Σ ⊂ R′^× makes R⟨x_u^{±1}; u ∈ Σ⟩ → R′ surjective with a d-element subset Σ_0 ⊂ Σ inducing an étale map X → 𝕋^d_Y; such Σ exist Zariski locally. For Z the generic fibre of Spf(R⟨x_u^{±1}; u ∈ Σ⟩), D_Σ(R′) := O_inf({Z_{m,e}}) is the formal completion of R⟨x_u^{±1}; u ∈ Σ⟩_{B⁺} → R′_C, isomorphic to R′_{B⁺}⟦x_u − u; u ∈ Σ ∖ Σ_0⟧; D_{Σ^n}(R′) is the completion along the diagonal of the (n+1)-fold product.
items.note: Printed with power-series variables for all u ∈ Σ (sourceIssues E32).

items.name: Čech–Alexander and de Rham complexes for infinitesimal crystals
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}. Let ℱ be a crystal in vector bundles over X/Y_{B⁺,inf}; let Z be a smooth affinoid adic space over Y_K with a closed immersion X_C → Z_C over Y_C; let Σ ⊂ R'^× be an enlarged framing. (1) The Čech–Alexander complex of ℱ for the covering D_Z(X) is the cosimplicial complex ℱ_{D_{Z^•}(X)}, with ℱ_{D_{Z^n}(X)} := lim_{m,e} ℱ(Z^n_{m,e}), a vector bundle over 𝒪_inf({Z^n_{m,e}}); for Z from Σ it is ℱ_{D_{Σ^•}(R')}. By Lemma 10.3 and vanishing of higher coherent cohomology on affinoids, RΓ(X/Y_{B⁺,inf}, ℱ) ≅ lim_{[n]∈Δ} ℱ_{D_{Z^n}(X)}, functorially in Z (and in enlarging Σ). (2) By [Guo21, Thm. 3.3.1], ℱ_{D_Z(X)} carries a natural flat connection ∇: ℱ_{D_Z(X)} → ℱ_{D_Z(X)} ⊗_{𝒪_Z} Ω^1_{Z/Y_K}, continuous for the natural topology; dR(ℱ_{D_Z(X)}) denotes the associated de Rham complex. For Z from Σ, dR(ℱ_{D_Σ(R')}) := dR(ℱ_{D_Z(X)}) is a Koszul complex since Ω^1_{R⟨x_u^{±1}⟩/R} is free.
items.note: The statement above leaves the top term of the de Rham complex unspecified; the paper prints Ω^d_{Z/Y_K}, while d is the relative dimension of X over Y and the complex is that of Z, of relative dimension |Σ| in the framed case (sourceIssues E36, added by the reviewer).

items.name: Rows of the Čech–Alexander/de Rham double complex are acyclic
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}. Let ℱ be a crystal in vector bundles over X/Y_{B⁺,inf}, Z a smooth affinoid adic space over Y_K with a closed immersion X_K → Z_K (X_C → Z_C). There is a natural double complex M^{a,b}_Σ := ℱ_{D_{Z^{a+1}}(X)} ⊗_{𝒪_{Z^{a+1}}} Ω^b_{Z^{a+1}/Y_K}, with Čech–Alexander (cosimplicial) direction a and de Rham direction b, functorial in ℱ and Z (and in enlarging Σ). For each b > 0 the cosimplicial complex M^{•,b}_Σ is acyclic (homotopic to zero).
items.note: Notational point, checked and deliberately not recorded as a mistake: Theorem 10.7 writes the Čech–Alexander direction as ℱ_{D_{Z^{a+1}}(X)} in the definition of M^{a,b}_Σ but as ℱ_{D_Z(X)^•} in its final sentence. The two denote the same cosimplicial object — the degree-a term is built from the (a+1)-fold self-product of Z — and no argument turns on the notation.

items.name: Columns of the double complex are quasi-isomorphic (Poincaré lemma)
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}. Let ℱ be a crystal in vector bundles over X/Y_{B⁺,inf}, Z a smooth affinoid adic space over Y_K with a closed immersion X_K → Z_K (X_C → Z_C). There is a natural double complex M^{a,b}_Σ := ℱ_{D_{Z^{a+1}}(X)} ⊗_{𝒪_{Z^{a+1}}} Ω^b_{Z^{a+1}/Y_K}, with Čech–Alexander (cosimplicial) direction a and de Rham direction b, functorial in ℱ and Z (and in enlarging Σ). Any map in Δ between [0] and [a] induces an isomorphism (quasi-isomorphism) of de Rham complexes M^{0,•}_Σ → M^{a,•}_Σ.
items.note: Two notational points, checked and deliberately not recorded as mistakes. (1) As in item 247, the degree-a term is the (a+1)-fold self-product of Z. (2) The paper says 'any degeneracy map [a] → [0] in Δ induces an isomorphism M^{0,•}_Σ → M^{a,•}_Σ'; the map M^{0,•}_Σ → M^{a,•}_Σ is the one induced by the projections Z^{a+1} → Z, which is what the proof uses (it forms dR(ℱ_{D_Z(X)}) → dR(ℱ_{D_{Z^{a+1}}(X)})), while the unique map [a] → [0] induces the diagonal in the other direction. The two maps are mutually inverse once either is an isomorphism, so the content is unaffected.

items.name: Čech–Alexander = de Rham for infinitesimal cohomology over B⁺_dR
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}. Let ℱ be a crystal in vector bundles over X/Y_{B⁺,inf}, Z a smooth affinoid adic space over Y_K with a closed immersion X_K → Z_K (X_C → Z_C). There is a natural double complex M^{a,b}_Σ := ℱ_{D_{Z^{a+1}}(X)} ⊗_{𝒪_{Z^{a+1}}} Ω^b_{Z^{a+1}/Y_K}, with Čech–Alexander (cosimplicial) direction a and de Rham direction b, functorial in ℱ and Z (and in enlarging Σ). Consequently the total complex of M^{a,b}_Σ is isomorphic to both M^{•,0}_Σ = lim_{[n]∈Δ} ℱ_{D_{Z^n}(X)} (≅ RΓ(X/Y_{B⁺,inf}, ℱ)) and M^{0,•}_Σ = dR(ℱ_{D_Z(X)}).
items.note: As in item 247: the degree-a term of the Čech–Alexander direction is built from the (a+1)-fold self-product of Z, which the paper's final display abbreviates differently. Not recorded as a mistake.

items.name: Infinitesimal cohomology via de Rham and Čech–Alexander complexes
items.statement: Setting of §10.1: K as before; A_inf = A_inf(O_C); B⁺_dR = 𝔹⁺_dR(O_C) = (A_inf[1/p])^∧_{ξ̃} (completion along ker θ̃, θ̃ = Hodge–Tate specialization); A_{inf,K} = A_inf ⊗_{W(k)} O_K; θ̃_K: A_{inf,K} → O_C; B⁺_{dR,e} = B⁺_dR/I^e; f: X → Y a smooth morphism of smooth formal O_K-schemes; X_{B_e}, Y_{B_e} the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_{dR,e}. Let ℱ be a crystal in vector bundles over X/Y_{B⁺,inf}. There are natural isomorphisms RΓ(X_{B⁺}, dR(ℱ_{X_{B⁺}})) ≅ RΓ(X/Y_{B⁺,inf}, ℱ) ≅ lim over affine opens U = Spf(R') ⊂ X with enlarged framings Σ of lim_{[n]∈Δ} ℱ_{D_{Σ^n}(R')} (using Z = X_K, resp. Z from Σ, in Theorem 10.7). Remark following it: RΓ(X_{B⁺}, dR(ℱ_{X_{B⁺}})) reduced mod I is the relative de Rham cohomology of the associated vector bundle with flat connection over X_C/Y_C.

items.name: Finiteness of relative B⁺_dR-infinitesimal cohomology
items.statement: Setting of §10.1: K as before; A_inf = A_inf(O_C); B⁺_dR = 𝔹⁺_dR(O_C) = (A_inf[1/p])^∧_{ξ̃} (completion along ker θ̃, θ̃ = Hodge–Tate specialization); A_{inf,K} = A_inf ⊗_{W(k)} O_K; θ̃_K: A_{inf,K} → O_C; B⁺_{dR,e} = B⁺_dR/I^e; f: X → Y a smooth morphism of smooth formal O_K-schemes; X_{B_e}, Y_{B_e} the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_{dR,e}. Assume X → Y is smooth and proper (and Y = Spf(R) affine, implicit). Let ℱ be a crystal in vector bundles on X/Y_{B⁺,inf}. Then RΓ(X/Y_{B⁺,inf}, ℱ) is a perfect R_{B⁺}-complex.

items.name: Divided power envelopes D_{pd,Σ}(R'), D_{pd,Σ,m}(R') and their map to D_Σ(R')
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}. For an enlarged framing Σ: D_{pd,Σ}(R') is the p-complete (p-adic) divided power envelope of R_{A_inf}⟨x_u^{±1}⟩ → R'_{O_C/p}; the surjection factors through R_{A_inf}⟨x_u^{±1}⟩ → R'_{O_C} with kernel J, and D_{pd,Σ}(R') is the p-completed PD envelope of J. D_{pd,Σ,m}(R') := quotient of the divided power algebra of J by {f^i/i!: f ∈ J, i ≥ m} (a finite, hence p-complete, R_{A_inf}⟨x_u^{±1}⟩-algebra); D_{pd,Σ,m}(R')[1/p] = D_{pd,Σ}(R')[1/p]/J^m = R_{A_inf}⟨x_u^{±1}⟩[1/p]/J^m. Taking lim_m gives D_{pd,Σ}(R') → D_Σ(R') ≅ (D_{pd,Σ}(R')[1/p])^∧_J, factoring through D_{pd,Σ}(R') ⊗̂_{A_{inf,K}} B⁺_dR := lim_m D_{pd,Σ}(R')[1/p]/ker(θ̃_K)^m. Similarly D_{pd,Σ^n}(R') is the p-complete PD envelope of R_{A_inf}⟨x_u^{±1}⟩^{⊗̂_{R_{A_inf}}(n+1)} → R'_{O_C}, mapping to D_{Σ^n}(R').

items.name: Infinitesimal crystals from crystalline crystals
items.statement: Setting of §10.1: K as before; A_inf = A_inf(O_C); B⁺_dR = 𝔹⁺_dR(O_C) = (A_inf[1/p])^∧_{ξ̃} (completion along ker θ̃, θ̃ = Hodge–Tate specialization); A_{inf,K} = A_inf ⊗_{W(k)} O_K; θ̃_K: A_{inf,K} → O_C; B⁺_{dR,e} = B⁺_dR/I^e; f: X → Y a smooth morphism of smooth formal O_K-schemes; X_{B_e}, Y_{B_e} the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_{dR,e}. There is a natural functor D_perf(X_{p=0,crys}) → D_perf(X/Y_{B⁺,inf}) whose restriction to Vect(X_{p=0,crys}) lands in Vect(X/Y_{B⁺,inf}). Locally (Convention 10.4, enlarged framing Σ) the associated crystal ℱ has value at D_{Σ^n}(R') equal to ℰ'(D_{pd,Σ^n}(R'), R'_{O_C/p}) ⊗^L_{D_{pd,Σ^n}(R')} D_{Σ^n}(R').
items.note: The statement above gives the corrected value; the paper prints the base change to D_Σ(R') in place of D_{Σ^n}(R') (sourceIssues E33).

items.name: A_{crys,K}, R_{A_crys} and two computations of relative crystalline cohomology
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}. A_{crys,K} denotes (abusing notation) the p-completed PD envelope of A_{inf,K} → O_C given by the O_K-linear extension of θ. R_{A_crys} := (R ⊗_{O_K} A_{crys,K})^∧_p, a p-completed PD thickening of R_{O_C/p} = R ⊗_{O_K} O_C/p. For a crystal in vector bundles ℰ' on (X_{p=0}/R)_crys, since X is a smooth lift of X_{p=0} over R (weakly final), RΓ((X_{p=0}/R)_crys, ℰ') is computed by [BdJ11, Thm. 2.12] either by the Čech–Alexander complex ℰ'_{D_{pd,X^•}(X_{p=0})} (p-completed PD thickenings of X_{p=0} → X^{×_Y(n+1)}) or by the relative de Rham complex dR(ℰ'_X, ∇_{X/Y}); similarly (by p-complete base change along (R → R/p) → (R_{A_crys} → R_{O_C/p})) for RΓ((X_{O_C/p}/R_{A_crys})_crys, ℰ'), and these map to the infinitesimal analogues of Construction 10.6.
items.note: A_{crys,K} is printed as the PD envelope for the O_K-linear extension of θ; it must be that of the Hodge–Tate specialization θ̃_K, consistently with the completions along ker(θ̃_K) in Proposition 10.11 (sourceIssues E34).

items.name: Crystalline vs infinitesimal cohomology over B⁺_dR
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}. Let ℰ' ∈ Vect(X_{p=0,crys}) and ℱ its associated infinitesimal crystal on X/Y_{B⁺,inf} (Proposition 10.10). There are natural isomorphisms of R_{B⁺}-complexes RΓ((X_{p=0}/R)_crys, ℰ') ⊗̂_R R_{B⁺} ≅ RΓ((X_{O_C/p}/R_{A_crys})_crys, ℰ') ⊗̂_{R_{A_crys}} R_{B⁺} ≅ RΓ((X/Y)_{B⁺,inf}, ℱ), where RΓ((X_{p=0}/R)_crys, ℰ') ⊗̂_R R_{B⁺} := (((RΓ((X_{p=0}/R)_crys, ℰ') ⊗_R R_{A_crys})^∧_p)[1/p])^∧_{ker θ̃_K} and RΓ((X_{O_C/p}/R_{A_crys})_crys, ℰ') ⊗̂_{R_{A_crys}} R_{B⁺} := (RΓ((X_{O_C/p}/R_{A_crys})_crys, ℰ')[1/p])^∧_{ker θ̃_K}.

items.name: De Rham cohomology of E vs infinitesimal cohomology
items.statement: Convention 10.4: R → R' is a smooth morphism of relative dimension d of smooth topologically finite type O_K-algebras, X = Spf(R') → Y = Spf(R); R_{B⁺}, R_{B_e} (and R'_{B⁺}, R'_{B_e}) are the completed base changes along O_K → A_{inf,K} → B⁺_dR, resp. → B⁺_{dR,e}. (Claim after Proposition 10.11) The construction is compatible with the cohomology of the underlying vector bundle E over X_K of Proposition 2.17 (where ℰ'[1/p] underlies a convergent crystal ℰ_conv on (X_{p=0}/W(k))_crys), giving a natural isomorphism dR(X_η, (E, ∇_{X_η/Y_η})) ⊗̂_{R_K} R_{B⁺} ≅ RΓ(X_{B⁺}, dR(ℱ_{X_{B⁺}})).

items.name: Admissible perfect prisms over (A_inf, [p]_q)
items.statement: Convention 10.12: (A, I) is a perfect prism which is p-completely flat over (A_inf, [p]_q), q = [ε] for a compatible system ε of p-power roots of unity in O_C^♭. Claim: for Y smooth over O_K, there is a basis of affinoid perfectoid spaces Spa(S,S⁺) of Y_{C,proét} such that A := A_inf(S,S⁺) satisfies Convention 10.12.

items.name: Theorem 10.13: filtered compatibility of the étale–crystalline comparison
items.statement: Fix a proper smooth morphism f: X → Y of smooth formal O_K-schemes (standing assumption of §10.2), Y = Spf(R). Let T be a crystalline ℤ_p-lisse sheaf on X_η with associated analytic prismatic F-crystal (ℰ, φ_ℰ). Let (A, I) ∈ Y_Δ be a perfect prism satisfying Convention 10.12 such that A ⊗_{W(k)} O_K admits a map from R compatible with R → Ā. Then the base change of the étale–crystalline comparison of Theorem 9.15 to 𝔹_dR(Ā) = A[1/p]^∧_I[1/I] underlies a filtered isomorphism RΓ_dR(X_η/Y_η, E) ⊗_{R_K} 𝔹_dR(Ā) ≅ RΓ(X_{Ā[1/p],ét}, T) ⊗_{ℤ_p(Spf(Ā)_η)} 𝔹_dR(Ā), where the right side carries the filtration induced by the I-adic filtration of A[1/p]^∧_I, and the left side the tensor product of the Hodge filtration on the relative de Rham cohomology of the filtered vector bundle with connection (E, ∇_{X_η/Y_η}, Fil^•) (Corollary 2.37, Proposition 2.17) with the filtration of 𝔹_dR(Ā).
items.note: Theorem 1.24 in the introduction omits properness of f (sourceIssues E4). T is a crystalline lisse Ẑ_p-sheaf here; Theorem 9.15, whose base change this is, is stated for the étale realization of a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes.

items.name: Sheaf-level filtered comparison with 𝒪𝔹_dR (Remark 10.14; source of Theorem 1.24)
items.statement: (Remark 10.14) The statement of Theorem 10.13 is functorial in the prism (A, I) ∈ Y_Δ together with the section R_K → A ⊗_{W(k)} O_K, hence gives an isomorphism of sheaves Rf_{dR,*}(E, ∇) ⊗_{𝒪_{Y_η}} 𝔹_dR|_{Spf(A)_η} ≅ Rf_{η,*}T ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_dR|_{Spf(A)_η}. Using the crystal condition of Rf_{p=0,crys,*}ℰ' and Griffiths transversality for the relative Hodge filtration on RΓ_dR(X_K/Y_K, E), there is a natural filtered isomorphism RΓ_dR(X_K/Y_K, E) ⊗_{R_K} 𝔹_dR(Ā) ⊗_{𝔹_dR(Ā)} 𝒪𝔹_dR(Ā) ≅ RΓ_dR(X_K/Y_K, E) ⊗_{R_K} 𝒪𝔹_dR(Ā) (second tensor product via the canonical map R_K → 𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y}(Ā)), whence a canonical filtered isomorphism of complexes on Y_{η,proét}: Rf_{dR,*}(E, ∇) ⊗_{𝒪_{Y_η}} 𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y} ≅ Rf_{η,*}T ⊗_{Ẑ_{p,Y_η}} 𝒪𝔹_{dR,Y} (f smooth proper).

items.name: Cohomology theories used in the proof of Theorem 10.13
items.statement: Let T be a crystalline ℤ_p-local system on X_η with associated analytic prismatic F-crystal (ℰ, φ_ℰ), (A, I) ∈ Y_Δ a perfect prism satisfying Convention 10.12, Y = Spf(R) smooth affine, and fix a lift R → A_{O_K} := A ⊗_{W(k)} O_K of R → Ā (by smoothness of R over O_K). Define: RΓ_Δ := RΓ((X_Ā/A)_Δ, ℰ); RΓ_ét := RΓ(X_{Ā[1/p],ét}, T); RΓ_crys := RΓ(X_{Ā/p}/A_crys(Ā/p), ℰ') with ℰ' the crystalline crystal on X_{p=0,crys} (Theorem 6.4), where A_crys(Ā/p) ≅ Δ_{Ā/p} is the p-complete PD envelope of A → A/(p, φ^{-1}(I)) and Ā/p is an A_crys(Ā/p)-algebra via A_crys(Ā/p) → A/(p, φ^{-1}(I)) ≅(φ) Ā/p (factorizing Frobenius of A_crys(Ā/p)/p; cf. [BL22a, Thm. 4.6.1, Ex. 4.6.9]); RΓ_inf := RΓ(X/Y_{B⁺,inf}, ℰ'') with ℰ'' from Proposition 10.10; RΓ_proét := RΓ(X_{Ā[1/p],proét}, 𝔹_dR(ℰ)); RΓ_dR := RΓ_dR(X_η/Y_η, E) (Hodge-filtered); the filtered de Rham complex dR(𝔹_dR(ℰ) ⊗ 𝒪𝔹_dR) := 𝔹_dR(ℰ) ⊗_{𝔹_dR} dR(𝒪𝔹_dR, d_{X_η/Y_η}) ≅ 𝒪𝔹_dR ⊗_{𝒪_{X_η}} dR(E, ∇_{X_η/Y_η}) ([Sch13, Rmk. 6.9, Thm. 7.6]) and RΓ_{proét-dR} := RΓ(X_{Ā[1/p],proét}, dR(𝔹_dR(ℰ) ⊗ 𝒪𝔹_dR)).

items.name: Commutative diagram of comparison isomorphisms over 𝔹_dR(Ā)
items.statement: In the setting of Construction 10.15 (f: X → Y proper smooth), there is a natural commutative diagram of isomorphisms of cohomology complexes over 𝔹_dR(Ā): γ_ét: RΓ_ét ⊗_{ℤ_p} 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_Δ ⊗_A 𝔹_dR(Ā); γ_crys: RΓ_crys ⊗_{A_crys(Ā/p)} 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_Δ ⊗_A 𝔹_dR(Ā); vertical maps RΓ_Δ ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_proét ← RΓ_inf ⊗_{R_{B⁺}} 𝔹_dR(Ā) ← RΓ_crys ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā); red (filtered) isomorphisms RΓ_ét ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_proét → RΓ_{proét-dR} ← RΓ_dR ⊗_{R_K} 𝔹_dR(Ā); and RΓ_dR ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_inf ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā); with two maps RΓ_inf ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā) ⇉ RΓ_proét (Čech–Alexander (2.b) and Koszul (3.b)) shown to agree (block (4)). In particular, the étale–crystalline comparison γ_crys^{-1} ∘ γ_ét underlies a natural filtered isomorphism after base change to 𝔹_dR(Ā).

items.name: Block (1): étale vs pro-étale de Rham period cohomology
items.statement: (Diagram (1) in the proof of Theorem 10.16) Using the φ-equivariant isomorphism T ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔸_inf[1/μ] ≅ 𝔸_inf(ℰ)[1/μ] of Lemma 3.13 and its base change T ⊗_{Ẑ_p} 𝔹_dR ≅ 𝔹_dR(ℰ), the triangle γ_ét: RΓ_ét ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_Δ ⊗_A 𝔹_dR(Ā), (1.a): RΓ_Δ ⊗_A 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_proét (restriction to perfect prisms (𝔸_inf(S[1/p],S), I) coming from affinoid perfectoids over X_{Ā[1/p]}), and (1.b): RΓ_ét ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_proét (defined in [Sch13, Thm. 8.8] via T → (T ⊗ 𝔸_inf)^a → 𝔸_inf(ℰ)^a; a filtered isomorphism by [Sch13, Thm. 8.8.(i)]) commutes; hence (1.a) is an isomorphism.
items.note: Printed text differs: (printed with 𝔸_crys)

items.name: Block (2): prismatic–crystalline vs infinitesimal comparison via Čech–Alexander complexes
items.statement: (Diagram (2)/(2') in the proof of Theorem 10.16) With A_{crys,K}(Ā/p) := p-completed PD envelope of A_{O_K} → Ā/p, R_{A_inf} := (R ⊗_{O_K} A_{inf,K})^∧_p ≅ (R ⊗_W A_inf)^∧_p, R_{A_crys} := p-complete PD envelope of R_{A_inf} → R_{O_C/p}, the lift R → A_{O_K} induces maps R_{A_inf} → A_{O_K}, R_{A_crys} → A_{crys,K}(Ā/p) (a map of PD thickenings over R_{O_C/p} → Ā/p), R_{B⁺} → 𝔹_dR(Ā); A_crys(Ā/p) → 𝔹_dR(Ā) factors through A_{crys,K}(Ā/p). For each affine U = Spf(R') ⊂ X with enlarged framing Σ, the square formed by γ_{crys,K} ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā), (1.a), (2.a): RΓ_{crys,K} ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_inf ⊗_{R_{B⁺}} 𝔹_dR(Ā) and (2.b): RΓ_inf ⊗ 𝔹_dR(Ā) → RΓ_proét (x_u ↦ Teichmüller lifts [(x_u, x_u^{1/p}, …)]) commutes on explicit Čech–Alexander complexes functorially in (U, Σ); γ_{crys,K}, (2.a) are local quasi-isomorphisms, (1.a) a global one, the top-right arrow is a global isomorphism (proper smoothness, finiteness of crystalline cohomology), hence (2.b) is a global quasi-isomorphism.

items.name: Block (3): infinitesimal vs de Rham vs pro-étale de Rham via Koszul complexes
items.statement: (Diagram (3) in the proof of Theorem 10.16) Let D̃_Σ(R') be the formal completion of (R⟨x_u^{±1}⟩ ⊗̂_R R')_{B⁺} → R'_C (value of 𝒪_inf at a weakly final object by Lemma 10.3), receiving maps from R'_{B⁺} and D_Σ(R'); Koszul functoriality gives isomorphisms dR(ℰ''_{D_Σ(R')}) ≅ dR(ℰ''_{D̃_Σ(R')}) ≅ dR(ℰ''_{R'_{B⁺}}) computing RΓ(U/Y_{B⁺,inf}, ℰ''). The generic fibre Spa(R'_{∞,Ā[1/p]}, R'^+_{∞,Ā}) → X_{Ā[1/p]} is a G = ℤ_p(1)^Σ-torsor with affinoid perfectoid source, so ([Sch13, Thm. 6.5], crystal property) pro-étale cohomology of 𝔹_dR(ℰ) and of 𝔹_dR(ℰ) ⊗ 𝒪𝔹_dR ⊗ Ω^i is computed by G-Koszul complexes; with [Sch13, Thm. 7.6, 8.8] this gives isomorphisms Kos_G(𝔹_dR(ℰ)(…)) → Tot Kos_G(dR(𝔹_dR(ℰ) ⊗ 𝒪𝔹_dR)) ← dR(E,∇) ⊗̂_R 𝔹_dR(Ā). The ring map R⟨x_u^{±1}⟩ → 𝔸_{inf,K}(…), x_u ↦ [(x_u, x_u^{1/p}, …)], yields a commutative diagram (as in the last paragraph of the proof of [BMS18, Thm. 13.1]) relating (3.a), (3.b) with the filtered isomorphisms (3.c), (3.d); hence all arrows are global isomorphisms underlying filtered isomorphisms.

items.name: Double complexes M_Σ^{a,b} (infinitesimal) and N_Σ^{a,b} (pro-étale) for block (4)
items.statement: (Diagram (4) in the proof of Theorem 10.16) ČA_{proét,Σ} := lim 𝔹_dR(ℰ)(Spa(R'_{∞,Ā[1/p]}, R'^+_{∞,Ā})^{×(n+1) over X_{Ā,η}}), ČA_{inf,Σ} := lim ℰ''(D_{Σ^n}(R')), Kos_{proét,Σ} := Kos_G(𝔹_dR(ℰ)(Spa(R'_{∞,Ā[1/p]}, R'^+_{∞,Ā}))), Kos_{inf,Σ} := dR(ℰ''_{D_Σ(R')}) ⊗̂_{R_{B⁺}} 𝔹_dR(Ā). Double complexes: M_Σ^{a,b} := ℰ''_{D_Σ(R')^a} ⊗_{(R⟨x_u^{±1}⟩)^{⊗̂_R(a+1)}} Ω^b_{R⟨x_u^{±1}⟩^{⊗̂_R(a+1)}/R} ⊗̂_{R'_{B⁺}} 𝔹_dR(Ā) and N_Σ^{a,b} := Kos^b_{G^{a+1}}(𝔹_dR(ℰ)(Spa(R'_{∞,Ā[1/p]}, R'^+_{∞,Ā})^{a+1})), with a natural map M_Σ → N_Σ which is (2.b) row-wise and (3.b) column-wise; truncations give a commutative diagram showing that (2.b) and (3.b) agree globally.

items.name: Rows of N_Σ are acyclic
items.statement: (Setting of the proof of Theorem 10.16) Let N_Σ^{•,•} be the double complex N_Σ^{a,b} := Kos^b_{G^{a+1}}(𝔹_dR(ℰ)(Z^a)), where Z^a := Spa(R'_{∞,Ā[1/p]}, R'^+_{∞,Ā})^{×_{X_{Ā,η}}(a+1)} is affinoid perfectoid, G = ℤ_p(1)^Σ, and R'_∞ is the p-complete base change of R' along R⟨x_u^{±1}⟩ → R⟨x_u^{±1/p^∞}⟩ (Σ an enlarged framing). For each b > 0 the row N_Σ^{•,b} is an acyclic cosimplicial complex.

items.name: Columns of N_Σ are quasi-isomorphic
items.statement: (Setting of the proof of Theorem 10.16) Let N_Σ^{•,•} be the double complex N_Σ^{a,b} := Kos^b_{G^{a+1}}(𝔹_dR(ℰ)(Z^a)), where Z^a := Spa(R'_{∞,Ā[1/p]}, R'^+_{∞,Ā})^{×_{X_{Ā,η}}(a+1)} is affinoid perfectoid, G = ℤ_p(1)^Σ, and R'_∞ is the p-complete base change of R' along R⟨x_u^{±1}⟩ → R⟨x_u^{±1/p^∞}⟩ (Σ an enlarged framing). Any map in Δ between [0] and [a] induces an isomorphism of Koszul complexes N_Σ^{0,•} → N_Σ^{a,•} (induced by the covering map Z^a → Z^0); each column computes RΓ(X_{Ā,η,proét}, 𝔹_dR(ℰ)).
items.note: Printed text differs: (printed: 'any degeneracy map [a] → [0]')

items.name: Total complex of N_Σ
items.statement: (Setting of the proof of Theorem 10.16) Let N_Σ^{•,•} be the double complex N_Σ^{a,b} := Kos^b_{G^{a+1}}(𝔹_dR(ℰ)(Z^a)), where Z^a := Spa(R'_{∞,Ā[1/p]}, R'^+_{∞,Ā})^{×_{X_{Ā,η}}(a+1)} is affinoid perfectoid, G = ℤ_p(1)^Σ, and R'_∞ is the p-complete base change of R' along R⟨x_u^{±1}⟩ → R⟨x_u^{±1/p^∞}⟩ (Σ an enlarged framing). The total complex of N_Σ^{a,b} is quasi-isomorphic to both N_Σ^{0,•} = Kos_{proét,Σ} and N_Σ^{•,0} = ČA_{proét,Σ}, compatibly with the map from M_Σ^{•,•}.

items.name: Witt vector affine Grassmannian
items.statement: The Witt vector affine Grassmannian Gr_{GL_r} is an increasing union of perfections of proper (projective) algebraic spaces Gr_n.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 9.9, p. 87, citing [Zhu17, Thm 0.1], [BS17, Thm 1.1, 8.3]

items.name: Points of qcqs algebraic spaces on products of rings (Bhatt)
items.statement: For a qcqs algebraic space X, X(∏_j A_j) → ∏_j X(A_j) is a bijection under Bhatt's algebraization hypotheses (via Tannaka duality/algebraization).

items.name: Crystalline cohomology of affines via de Rham complexes of lifts
items.statement: For a smooth lift, crystalline cohomology of an affine in the p-completed setting is computed by the de Rham complex of the lift (Bhatt–de Jong).

items.name: Crystalline and infinitesimal cohomology over B⁺_dR (BMS)

routes.title: Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants, Part II: prismatic F-crystals and crystalline local systems on smooth formal schemes
routes.brief: First prerequisite: Prismatic cohomology: relative, absolute, Nygaard and log variants (PrismaticCohomology). This Part II starts where PR.7 stops: PR.7 proves the Bhatt–Scholze equivalence for Spf(O_K); this roadmap extends it to smooth p-adic formal schemes over O_K (K discretely valued, possibly ramified) and derives the relative C_crys conjecture with coefficients. Final theorems, stated with the corrections recorded in sourceIssues: (A) Theorem A: the étale realization T : Vect^{an,φ}(X_Δ) → Loc^crys_{Z_p}(X_η) is an equivalence between analytic prismatic F-crystals and crystalline Z_p-local systems in Faltings' sense; (B) Theorem 5.10: analytic prismatic F-crystals embed fully faithfully into D^φ_perf(X_Δ) via pushforward at Breuil–Kisin-type prisms and base change; (C) comparisons with coefficients: weak étale comparison (Theorem 6.1), absolute and relative crystalline comparison (Theorem 6.4, Corollaries 6.8, 6.14); (D) Poincaré duality for prismatic pushforwards of crystals in perfect complexes, trace-free (Theorem 7.8, with f_*O_X = O_Y) and trace-normalized (Theorem 7.16, for smooth X, Y), and p-adic Poincaré duality for crystalline local systems (Corollary 1.17); (E) Frobenius isogeny: Rf_{Δ,*}E is a prismatic F-crystal in perfect complexes for f smooth proper (Theorem 8.1); (F) strong étale comparison Rf_{η,*}T(E) ⊗ 𝔸_inf[1/μ] ≅ 𝔸_inf(Rf_{Δ,*}E)[1/μ] (Theorem 9.1), the étale–crystalline comparison over 𝔹_crys (Theorem 9.15) and its filtered compatibility after 𝔹_dR (Theorem 10.13, f proper); (G) Theorem B: for f : X → Y smooth proper of smooth formal O_K-schemes and T crystalline, R^i f_{η,*}T is crystalline, associated with R^i f_{s,crys,*}E_s; Corollary C for geometric cohomology H^i(X_C, T). Cover every construction on the way: analytic prismatic crystals and F-crystals (Definitions 3.1, 3.5, with Proposition 3.7 for X flat over O_K), the étale and crystalline realizations, the lattice realization Φ with Ξ = φ*E ⊗ 𝔹⁺_dR, the Fargues-type full faithfulness, the gluing construction of M_S over 𝒴 = Spa(Δ_{S,perf}) ∖ V(p,I) with its annuli 𝒴_[a,b] and the Beilinson-fibre-square descent (Proposition 4.20), perfections of Laurent F-crystals and their arc-descent, Hodge–Tate crystals and their Higgs cohomology, base change and pushforward of crystals in perfect complexes, cup products and Frobenius structures on pushforwards, the finite-étale prismatic trace, the arc-local analysis of §9 over A = ∏ A_inf(V_j), and the relative infinitesimal site over 𝔹⁺_dR with its Čech–Alexander and de Rham complexes (§10). No roadmap plans Drinfeld–Mathew descent for analytic vector bundles, the higher-dimensional Breuil–Kisin prisms of Du–Liu–Moon–Shimizu, or Tian's Hodge–Tate crystal duality, so this roadmap owns them. Import: PrismaticCohomology PR.0–PR.8 (prisms, Bhatt–Scholze comparisons, Nygaard/Frobenius isogeny, étale comparison, Bhatt–Lurie absolute site and Hodge–Tate stack, PR.7's F-crystals over O_K); Integral A_inf cohomology (AInfCohomology AI.0–AI.5: BKF modules, Fargues' theorem); P-adic Hodge theory (PadicHodgeTheory P8 period sheaves) and its Part II on crystalline local systems (PadicHodgeTheoryPartIIRelativeCrystallineLocalSystems); Crystalline cohomology (CrystallineCohomology CR.1–CR.3); PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology for convergent isocrystals and Xu/Shiho; Cohomology comparisons (CohomologyComparisons CP.2–CP.3); the arc-topology roadmap (ArcTopologyAndDescent); RefinedTraceMethods RT.3b (Beilinson fibre square); RelativeFarguesFontaine RF0/RF4 (Kedlaya algebraization, Beauville–Laszlo); GeometricSatakeAndFusion GS0 (Witt Grassmannian). Every definition gets functoriality, base change, tensor/dual and Frobenius API and at least three unit tests, for example: the unit object and Breuil–Kisin twists O_Δ{n} ↦ Z_p(n); X = Spf O_K recovering Bhatt–Scholze; X = Spec k showing why Proposition 3.7 needs flatness; a p-divisible group's Dieudonné crystal; the trace in relative dimension 0; and an elliptic-curve family for Theorem B. Supply a suggested Lean file.
routes.reason: PR.7 proves the equivalence of prismatic F-crystals and crystalline lattices only for Spf(O_K); the higher-dimensional equivalence, the calculus of prismatic F-crystals in perfect complexes (comparisons with coefficients, Poincaré duality, Frobenius isogeny, strong étale comparison) and the relative C_crys conjecture are new layers in the direction of PrismaticCohomology.

routes.title: P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison, Part II: crystalline local systems on smooth formal schemes
routes.brief: First prerequisite: P-adic Hodge theory and geometric comparison (PadicHodgeTheory), whose P8 constructs the relative period sheaves (𝔸_inf, 𝔹⁺_dR, O𝔹_dR, 𝔸_crys, 𝔹_crys) and Scholze's relative de Rham comparison. This Part II adds crystalline local systems on smooth p-adic formal schemes over O_K (K discretely valued, possibly ramified). Final theorems: Faltings' definition of weakly crystalline and crystalline lisse Ẑ_p-sheaves (Definition 2.31), associated with filtered F-isocrystals on X_s; Proposition 2.29 (for quasi-compact X): Γ((X_{p=0}/V_0)_conv, E)[1/p] ≅ Γ(X_{η,proét}, 𝔹_crys(E)), Frobenius-equivariantly and filtered after ⊗K; Corollaries 2.30 and 2.35 (quasi-compact X): filtered F-isocrystals embed fully faithfully into filtered φ-𝔹_crys-bundles, and crystalline sheaves up to isogeny embed fully faithfully into filtered F-isocrystals; Proposition 2.36 and Corollary 2.37: E ⊗ O𝔹_dR ≅ 𝔹_dR(E) ⊗ O𝔹_dR filtered and horizontally, so crystalline implies de Rham; Proposition 2.38: weakly crystalline implies crystalline, via the Liu–Zhu criterion. Cover the K-linear sheaves 𝔹_{crys,K} and their filtration (Definitions 2.21, 2.23, Lemma 2.22 with the relative fundamental exact sequence), 𝔹_crys(E) and 𝔹_dR(E) for an F-isocrystal and their filtrations (Definition 2.25, Construction 2.28, independence for lifts compatible with θ), unramified models of framed formal schemes (Lemma 2.9), and the Tan–Tong, Shimizu and Brinon inputs. Correct the invariant computation in the proof of Proposition 2.29 for ramified K (sourceIssues E9). Import: CrystallineCohomology CR.1 (crystals, F-isocrystals), PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology (convergent isocrystals, Berthelot's equivalence), AdicSpacesPartII R4 (pro-étale site), PadicHodgeTheory R06.1–R06.2, P8. The prismatic characterisation (Theorem A) belongs to PrismaticCohomologyPartIICrystallineLocalSystems, which imports this roadmap. Unit tests: X = Spf O_K recovering crystalline representations; Q_p(1) with its filtered φ-module; a non-quasi-compact counterexample showing why quasi-compactness is assumed. Supply a suggested Lean file.
routes.reason: PadicHodgeTheory plans period rings, period sheaves and Scholze's relative comparison but not Faltings' crystalline local systems on formal schemes, the sheaves 𝔹_crys(E) attached to filtered F-isocrystals, or the full faithfulness of crystalline local systems into filtered F-isocrystals; these are p-adic Hodge theory independent of prisms, so they form a Part II of that roadmap which the prismatic Part II imports.

routes.title: The arc-topology and descent for étale cohomology
routes.brief: This route adds a consumer to the new roadmap proposed by the extractions of Bhatt–Mathew (PAPER-BHATT-MATHEW-21) and Bhatt–Scholze (PAPER-BHATT-SCHOLZE-17), and follows their brief: plan the arc-topology and the descent theorems it yields for étale cohomology. Guo–Reinecke need its p-complete version: arc_p-covers of p-complete rings detected on rank ≤ 1 valuation rings, arc-local rings as products of such valuation rings, and arc_p-descent for S ↦ RΓ_ét(Spec S[1/p], F) with torsion F (Bhatt–Mathew Cor. 6.17), together with the comparison of étale cohomology of Spec S[1/p] and Spa S[1/p] for perfectoid S (Scholze). Import perfectoid rings from PerfectoidSpaces and étale foundations from SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2. Unit tests: a product of rank-one valuation rings as an arc-cover, a rank-two valuation ring, and descent along S → ∏ V_j.
routes.reason: The arc-topology is not in the atlas; the new roadmap proposed by the Bhatt–Mathew and Bhatt–Scholze extractions is its owner, and this route adds the p-complete descent statements Guo–Reinecke use.

routes.title: Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations, Part II: relative birational geometry in positive and mixed characteristic
routes.brief: This route adds one item to the Part II of Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations on relative birational geometry in positive and mixed characteristic, proposed by the extraction of Bhatt et al. (PAPER-BHATT-ETAL-23), which already plans Bhatt's Cohen–Macaulayness of absolute integral closures. Guo–Reinecke use two of its statements: for a p-complete regular (more generally excellent) ring R, the p-completed absolute integral closure R⁺ is perfectoid, and for R regular R⁺ is flat over R (Bhatt, arXiv 2008.08070). Import perfectoid rings from PerfectoidSpaces P1 and prismatic inputs from PrismaticCohomology PR.0–PR.2. Unit tests: Z_p⁺, a two-dimensional regular local ring, and a non-flat example over a non-regular ring.
routes.reason: Bhatt's theorems on absolute integral closures are already routed by the Bhatt et al. extraction to this proposed Part II; routing the paper's use there keeps one owner.

Convergent isocrystals (Ogus), Berthelot's equivalence of F-isocrystals with bundles with convergent connection, Xu's higher direct images and the Ogus–Shiho comparison of convergent and rational crystalline cohomology are the analytic coefficient theory of RD.3 (restriction to convergent isocrystals), RD.5 (finiteness and duality) and RD.7 (crystalline comparison); the paper's §2.2 and Theorem 6.13 are a source for those layers.

Kedlaya's algebraicity of vector bundles on Spa(W(R⁺)) ∖ V(p,[ϖ]) and the freeness/projectivity of φ-modules over products of valuation rings belong with RF0's integral period space 𝒴 and RF4's vector-bundle patching.

CP.3 builds the canonical B_dR⁺ deformation by the infinitesimal embedding system of BMS1 §13; Guo's infinitesimal cohomology over B_dR⁺ is the general relative form of that construction, and this paper is a source for it.

H3 owns traces and Poincaré duality in the classical adic étale theory; the Berkovich–Zavyalov trace for smooth proper rigid spaces is the general-dimensional form of that trace, which this paper uses to normalize the prismatic trace.
